key: Hiring a cook for a dhaba. A general
name: ch07_dhaba_cook_three_tests
alt: A dhaba owner tests a new cook three ways, from basic chopping to Punjabi dishes to his own dal makhani, while a helper brings ingredients in the kitchen behind.
scene: A wide view of a busy highway dhaba kitchen, shown as three stations from left to right like steps of a funnel that gets narrower. LEFT station: a broad steel table where the candidate cook, a lean man in his 30s with a white vest, checked gamchha on his shoulder and a confident grin, chops onions, boils water and fries pakoras at once, a small ticked checklist pinned above. MIDDLE station: a narrower counter with only Punjabi dishes, a tray of sarson ka saag, rotis and chole, the same cook concentrating, sleeves rolled up. RIGHT station: a single small table where the dhaba owner, a stout Sikh man in his 50s with a turban and a ledger tucked under his arm, tastes one spoon of dal makhani with closed eyes, two regular truck-driver customers peering over his shoulder waiting for his verdict. In the background behind all three stations, a young helper in shorts carries a basket of tomatoes and butter from a storeroom door to the cook's counter, with a dotted arrow showing the path, and a small inset bubble shows the cook actually reaching for those exact ingredients. Warm yellow light from hanging bulbs, steam rising from pots, lively but focused mood. Labels: "GENERAL" above the left station, "DOMAIN" above the middle station, "TASK" above the right station.

key: like a cricket commentator guessing
name: ch07_commentator_next_ball
alt: A nervous new cricket commentator imagines dozens of possible deliveries while a calm veteran beside him expects only three.
scene: Inside a glass-fronted commentary box above a cricket ground, two commentators sit side by side at a desk with microphones and headphones, the pitch visible through the window behind them where a fast bowler is mid run-up. LEFT: a young new commentator in his early 20s, crisp blazer slightly too big for him, eyes wide and sweat on his brow, gripping his notes; above his head a crowded thought cloud bursts with dozens of tiny ball icons going everywhere: bouncer, yorker, slower ball, wide, googly, beamer, no-ball, scattered in all directions. RIGHT: a grey-haired veteran commentator in his 60s, relaxed in a cardigan, one hand resting calmly on the desk, a cup of tea beside him and a small notebook open on the bowler's past overs; his tidy thought cloud holds just three neat ball icons with one, the outswinger, slightly larger. A thin arrow from the bowler's hand through the window points to the veteran's cloud, where the ball he expected is circled. Afternoon sunlight floods the stadium, the crowd a soft blur, mood light and good-humoured. Labels: "HIGH PERPLEXITY" above the young commentator, "LOW PERPLEXITY" above the veteran.

key: two suitors answer the same question
name: ch07_exam_swayamvar_form
alt: Three panels: a large multiple-choice entrance exam hall, two suitors answering the same question before an audience that votes, and a clerk checking a form filled in block letters.
scene: A three-panel illustration separated by thin vertical lines, read left to right. LEFT panel: a huge exam hall with rows of students in school uniforms bent over OMR answer sheets, filling bubbles with pencils; a wall clock above and an invigilator walking the aisle; one sheet in the foreground shows four bubbles per question and a neat final score in a box. MIDDLE panel: a festive royal-court stage with marigold garlands; two young suitors in sherwanis stand at twin podiums, both answering the same question shown on a scroll held by a herald; a large seated audience below raises coloured paddles to pick one, and a tally board at the side shows rows of past duels with ticks adding up. RIGHT panel: a government office counter where an elderly clerk with round spectacles and a sleeveless sweater checks a printed form with a ruler, ticking boxes mechanically; the form's instruction line reads "BLOCK LETTERS" and the applicant's entries are in tall capitals with no overwriting, a rubber stamp waiting beside. Each panel has even, clear daylight; the mood moves from tense, to festive, to bureaucratic calm. Labels: "MMLU" above the left panel, "ARENA" above the middle panel, "IFEVAL" above the right panel.

key: ratings can be bought, and reviewers
name: ch07_restaurant_three_signals
alt: A young woman deciding on a restaurant checks an app rating, a friend's advice and a food blogger, and goes only when all three agree.
scene: A street at dusk outside a modest restaurant with a lit signboard and a glass door, framed as a medium shot. In the centre foreground stands a young woman in her late 20s in a kurta and jeans, phone in hand, weighing her decision with a thoughtful tilt of the head. Three signals surround her. LEFT: her phone screen enlarged in an inset bubble shows a food-delivery app listing with a big star rating "4.6", a picture of an enormous, elaborately plated thali, and a shady figure in the corner of the bubble slipping a banknote to a reviewer. CENTRE-RIGHT: her old friend, a man in his 30s with a backpack, stands beside her and points at the restaurant, saying something earnest; a small thought bubble above him shows only two visits marked on a tiny calendar. FAR RIGHT: a food blogger in a cap, holding a ring light and a camera, gives a thumbs-up as he walks out of the door. Faint dotted lines run from all three signals to a small checklist floating above the woman's head, three boxes all ticked, and she steps toward the door. Warm evening light, glowing shop windows, cheerful everyday mood. Labels: "RATING" near the phone bubble, "FRIEND" near the friend, "BLOGGER" near the blogger.

key: A general MBBS exam vs a cardiology
name: ch07_mbbs_vs_cardiology_exam
alt: A wide general medical exam paper covering many subjects beside a narrower cardiology exam that goes deep on the heart and borrows a few general questions.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves set in exam halls of a medical college. LEFT panel: a long table covered with a broad, thin question paper that fans out into many short sections, each marked with a small icon (a heart, a kidney, a bone, a brain, a pill bottle, a baby), and a young medical graduate in a white coat, mid 20s, glasses pushed up, skimming quickly across all of them with a pencil. RIGHT panel: a smaller desk with a thick, narrow question booklet where every page shows detailed drawings of the heart, ECG strips and valve diagrams; an older doctor in her 30s, stethoscope around her neck, studies one page intently, deep in thought. A small arrow curves from three of the general icons in the left panel into the right booklet's front pages, showing a few general questions borrowed into the specialist exam. On the right desk, beside the booklet, sits a multiple-choice answer sheet with A to D bubbles, and through the window behind her a faint hospital ward with a real patient in a bed hints at open-ended clinical work the paper does not cover. Calm fluorescent light, serious academic mood. Labels: "BROAD" above the left panel, "DEEP" above the right panel.

key: the plot survives but jokes and idioms
name: ch07_film_dubbing_translation
alt: A cinema audience reacts to three versions of a film: a confusing machine-dubbed foreign film, a careful human dub, and an original Hindi film full of local detail.
scene: A three-panel illustration, each panel showing a small cinema screen above two or three seated viewers seen from behind and slightly side-on. LEFT panel: a foreign action film dubbed by a machine; on screen a cowboy character speaks, and his speech bubble holds jumbled symbols and a question mark; in the seats a middle-aged couple turn to each other in confusion and a teenager scratches his head, popcorn forgotten. MIDDLE panel: the same foreign film dubbed by people; a small inset shows a dubbing studio with a voice artist in headphones at a microphone and a translator beside him checking a script with a red pen; the audience below is smiling and following along. RIGHT panel: an original Hindi film; the screen shows a lively family courtyard with a wedding mandap, rangoli and relatives in bright clothes; the audience laughs heartily, one grandmother wiping happy tears, clearly catching every cultural joke. A thin arrow runs left to right beneath the three panels, the quality improving step by step. Dim cinema lighting with each screen glowing, playful mood. Labels: "MACHINE DUB" above the left panel, "HUMAN DUB" above the middle panel, "NATIVE" above the right panel.

key: Log-likelihood scoring is like a viva
name: ch07_viva_nod_vs_written
alt: In a viva a student nods slightly at option B as the examiner reads choices, but in a written exam the same student writes a vague sentence instead of B and scores zero.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same nervous college student in both halves (about 19, loose shirt, untidy hair, ballpoint behind his ear). LEFT panel: a small viva room with a wooden table; a bearded examiner in his 50s with half-moon glasses reads four options aloud from a card, A, B, C and D printed as big floating letters between them; the student sits across, and as the examiner says B the student's head tips forward in a tiny nod, shown with two small curved motion lines; the examiner raises an eyebrow and makes a tick next to B on his notepad. RIGHT panel: a quiet exam hall; the same student sits alone at a desk with an answer sheet that has one empty square answer box; instead of writing a letter inside it, he has written a long wobbly sentence that spills out of the box and trails off with dots; a big red zero has been stamped on the sheet by an unseen hand, and the student stares at it, deflated. Left side has warm, intimate lamp light; right side has cool, flat daylight. Labels: "LOG-LIKELIHOOD" above the left panel, "GENERATION" above the right panel, "0" in red on the answer sheet.

key: A newspaper fact-checking desk.
name: ch07_fact_check_desk_ragas
alt: At a newspaper fact-checking desk, an editor traces each sentence of a reporter's story to his notes, checks the headline is answered, and sees whether the best notes were on top.
scene: A cluttered newspaper office at night seen from slightly above a long wooden fact-checking desk lit by green-shaded lamps. LEFT: a young reporter in his 20s, sleeves rolled up and lanyard around his neck, hands over a typed story and a messy stack of notebook pages. CENTRE: a sharp-eyed senior fact-checker in her 40s with reading glasses on a chain and a red pencil behind her ear lays the story beside the notes; thin coloured threads run from each sentence of the story to the exact note page it came from, and one sentence has no thread, circled in red. Above the story, a headline strip asks a question, and a small check mark shows the story answers it rather than something else. RIGHT: the pile of notes is drawn as a vertical stack; the most useful pages glow softly near the top while a crucial page lies buried near the bottom with a small arrow pulling it upward, and beside the stack a short checklist on a pinned card lists the facts the ideal story needs, one box still empty. Behind them, a robot-like assistant clerk with a clipboard waits as if ready to do this checking itself. Warm lamplight against dark windows, focused late-night mood. Labels: "FAITHFUL" above the threads, "RELEVANT" beside the headline, "RECALL" beside the checklist.

key: train a team of TAs on one narrow skill
name: ch07_professor_vs_trained_tas
alt: A slow professor grades answer sheets one at a time, while a row of teaching assistants trained on his samples each quickly check one narrow question across thousands of sheets.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in a university staff room. LEFT panel: an elderly professor in his 60s with a tweed jacket and wild white hair sits at a heavy desk, reading one answer sheet slowly with a magnifying glass; a tall unmarked pile towers beside him, a wall clock shows many hours passing, and his face shifts between a smile and a frown in two small mood icons floating above him. RIGHT panel: a long table with five young teaching assistants in college T-shirts and ID cards, each with a single coloured stamp reading only yes or no; each TA checks just one narrow thing on sheets sliding past on a conveyor-like line of trays, working fast and in sync. Pinned on a board behind them are a few of the professor's graded sample sheets they learned from. At the far right end, the professor stands with a cup of tea, re-checking a tiny handful of sheets, and a small balance scale beside him shows his marks agreeing with the TAs' totals. Bright, busy afternoon light on the right; dim, slow lamp light on the left. Labels: "RAGAS" above the left panel, "ARES" above the right panel, "HUMAN CHECK" beside the professor at the far right.

key: A ghostwriter audition. Two trainee
name: ch07_ghostwriter_audition
alt: Two trainee ghostwriters and one experienced staff writer answer the same prompts while an editor marks each answer for correctness and for sounding like a short social post.
scene: A small publishing office set up like an audition. In the foreground three writing desks stand side by side, each with a typewriter-like laptop and a growing stack of finished pages. LEFT desk: a young trainee in her early 20s, plain kurta, earnest and fast, a nameplate card on the desk. MIDDLE desk: a second trainee, a young man with a neat beard and a hoodie, who keeps glancing at a sticky note of feedback pinned to his screen. RIGHT desk: an experienced staff writer in his 40s with a waistcoat, writing long, formal pages that pile up high. All three are answering the same prompts drawn from a big glass bowl of folded slips on a stool in front. In the background, an editor in her 30s with a pen in her hair sits at a raised desk holding one page, with two rubber stamps in front of her: one with a tick, one with a small speech-bubble icon for style. A thought bubble above her shows a short, friendly social-media post versus a thick academic thesis, the thesis crossed out. Clean morning office light, friendly competitive mood. Labels: "SFT" on the left desk card, "DPO" on the middle desk card, "INSTRUCT" on the right desk card.

key: one delivery boy per tiffin
name: ch07_dabbawala_batch_vs_single
alt: One delivery boy on a bicycle carries a single tiffin through traffic, while dabbawalas load a huge crate of sorted tiffins onto a shared train.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, set in a busy Mumbai morning. LEFT panel: a single delivery boy, about 18, in a T-shirt and helmet, pedals a bicycle through dense traffic with one steel tiffin hanging from the handlebar; behind him a long line of other delivery boys, each with one tiffin, stretches into the distance, and a big clock tower above shows the time ticking away. RIGHT panel: a railway platform where several dabbawalas in white kurtas and Gandhi caps load long wooden crates packed with hundreds of colourful tiffins into a local train's luggage compartment; one older dabbawala reads the coloured code marks painted on tiffin lids and sorts them into the right crate with quick hands; a small counter painted on the crate reads "300". A thin arrow from the right panel's crate leads off toward many office buildings on the horizon, each receiving tiffins. Bright morning sun, dusty air, energetic mood. Labels: "ONE BY ONE" above the left panel, "BATCHED" above the right panel.

key: A board-exam evaluation centre.
name: ch07_evaluation_centre_packets
alt: At an exam evaluation centre, answer sheets bundled in packets go to ten examiners at once, and marks land in the right rows of the register even when examiners finish in a different order.
scene: A large hall in a school used as a board-exam evaluation centre, seen from a high corner. In the centre a supervisor in her 50s, cotton saree and spectacles, stands at a trolley stacked with answer sheets tied into small bundles of five with string, each bundle tagged with roll numbers. Around her, ten examiners sit at separate desks in a ring, each marking a bundle: some young, some grey-haired, men and women in shirts and sarees, red pens moving. Examiner number 7, a quick young man, is already walking his finished bundle back while examiner number 2, an older teacher, is still halfway, shown by a small partially filled progress bar above each head. On the right a long open register on a table shows rows by roll number, and thin dotted arrows from each finished bundle go to the exact matching rows, not to the next empty line. One sheet near the register has a smudged, unreadable mark; instead of halting the hall, a clerk simply writes a dash in that row with a small note card reading "absent". Ceiling fans turn, afternoon light through tall windows, calm and orderly mood. Labels: "THREADS" above the ring of examiners, "REGISTER" above the book, "NONE" beside the dash.

key: A naive stall boils one cup at a time
name: ch08_chai_stall_latency_throughput
alt: At a railway platform, a naive chai stall boils one cup at a time in a huge pot on a crowded counter while a skilled stall serves a crowd quickly from compact kettles.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves at the same railway platform just as a long train pulls in and passengers spill out. LEFT panel: a naive chai stall where a flustered young vendor in a vest and lungi stirs one single cup's worth of tea inside an enormous aluminium pot that hogs the whole counter; other kettles and cups are pushed to the very edge, one about to fall; a long impatient queue of passengers waves money, and the first passenger at the front, a businessman with a briefcase, taps his wristwatch. RIGHT panel: an experienced chaiwala in his 50s with a moustache and a checked shirt works a tidy counter with two small kettles on compact stoves, pouring a long stream of tea into a neat row of clay cups at once; passengers take cups and walk off smiling, and a small tally board on the stall pillar shows many cups served. Three small icons float over each stall: a stopwatch over the first customer, a row of cups for cups per minute, and a ruler across the counter for space used, large and red on the left, small and green on the right. Morning light slanting through the station roof, steam everywhere, bustling mood. Labels: "LATENCY" by the stopwatch, "THROUGHPUT" by the cups, "MEMORY" by the ruler.

key: Antakshari: each singer must wait
name: ch08_antakshari_one_after_another
alt: A family plays antakshari in a circle; everyone reads the first song together, but each singer must wait for the previous song's last word before starting.
scene: A warm living room at night during a family get-together, seen from slightly above. About ten relatives of all ages sit in a circle on durries and cushions: a grandmother in a white saree, two teenagers with phones set aside, an uncle with a harmonium, an aunt clapping a rhythm, a small child on a lap. In the centre on a low table lies a printed song sheet, and every person leans in to read it at the same moment, shown by many short sight lines converging on the sheet. Around the circle, a chain of speech bubbles passes from one singer to the next: each bubble holds a few musical notes and ends with a single big highlighted letter, and a curved arrow carries that last letter to the next singer, who waits with mouth closed and a finger raised until it arrives. Only one person sings at a time, glowing slightly; the rest wait. At the doorway, three more cousins arrive with snacks, and a small thought bubble above them shows the chain moving no faster with them. Yellow lamp light, festive garlands on the wall, joyful but patient mood. Labels: "PROMPT" on the song sheet, "ONE TOKEN AT A TIME" along the curved arrow.

key: A junior clerk and a senior officer
name: ch08_junior_clerk_senior_officer
alt: A junior clerk quickly drafts five lines of a form; a senior officer checks them in one glance, ticks three, crosses out the fourth and writes the correct line himself.
scene: Inside a government office with tall steel cupboards, files tied with red tape and a ceiling fan, a medium shot of two desks pushed together. LEFT: a junior clerk in his early 20s, half-sleeve shirt and a pen behind his ear, scribbles quickly on a long printed form, filling five lines in a burst; small speed lines trail from his pen and a tiny stopwatch above him shows only seconds. RIGHT: a senior officer in his late 50s, grey hair, safari suit and reading glasses, holds the same form and looks over all five lines in a single sweep, a wide fan-shaped glance drawn from his eyes across the page. On the enlarged form between them, lines one, two and three carry green ticks, line four is crossed out in red with the correct line written neatly beside it in the officer's handwriting, and line five is struck off as no longer needed. A small balance icon floating above shows one glance from the senior equal in time to one line of his own writing. In the background, a pile of finished forms grows tall, faster than a lone officer could manage. Afternoon light through barred windows, efficient, slightly humorous mood. Labels: "DRAFT" above the junior clerk, "VERIFY" above the senior officer.

key: A chef with a tiny counter and a big
name: ch08_chef_storeroom_trips
alt: A chef with a tiny counter walks back and forth to a storeroom with full trays, versus a chef who chops, fries and plates a handful of onions at a time with a small salt note.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same restaurant layout in cross-section: a tiny steel counter at the front and a large storeroom with shelves at the back, connected by a corridor. The same chef appears in both, a man in his 30s in a white chef's jacket and cap. LEFT panel: the chef carries a big full tray of chopped onions down the corridor to the storeroom, then back again to fry, then back again; his path is drawn as many long looping footprints going back and forth, he is sweaty and tired, and a counter on the wall marks many trips. RIGHT panel: the chef has only a small handful of onions on his counter, chopping, frying in a small kadhai and plating in one smooth sequence, with a little notepad pinned beside the stove showing a running note of salt added so far; just a few short trips to the storeroom are drawn, each for the next handful, with a small stack of finished plates growing. Clean kitchen light, steam rising from the kadhai, calm efficient mood on the right versus frantic on the left. Labels: "NAIVE" above the left panel, "FLASHATTENTION" above the right panel, "RUNNING NOTE" beside the notepad.

key: A wedding catering job too big for one
name: ch08_wedding_cooks_three_splits
alt: Three ways four cooks share a wedding job: each serving a quarter of the guests, a line passing plates from dal to rotis, and all four stirring one giant pot of biryani.
scene: A three-panel illustration of a large wedding kitchen tent with strings of lights, read left to right, the same four cooks in each panel (two men and two women in aprons, different ages). LEFT panel: four identical cooking stations, each cook with a complete set of pots for the full menu, each serving their own group of guests seated at separate tables; a small guest map shows the crowd split into four colour zones. MIDDLE panel: a straight assembly line; cook one ladles dal onto a plate, slides it to cook two who adds sabzi, then cook three adds hot rotis, and cook four garnishes and hands the plate to a waiter; arrows show plates moving down the line. RIGHT panel: one gigantic biryani handi over a wide fire, the four cooks standing around it, each stirring one quarter of the pot with a long ladle; the pot is divided by faint dotted lines into four slices, and a curved arrow shows them combining at the end. In each panel small speech-bubble lines between cooks show how often they must talk, few on the left, more in the middle, constant on the right. Golden evening light, festive and busy mood. Labels: "DATA" above the left panel, "PIPELINE" above the middle panel, "TENSOR" above the right panel.

key: Four identical UPI counters at a busy
name: ch08_petrol_pump_four_counters
alt: At a busy petrol pump, four identical QR payment counters each take customers at once, and an inset shows an app too large to fit on one phone.
scene: A wide shot of a busy roadside petrol pump at evening rush hour, with scooters, autos and cars queued under a bright canopy. Along the front stand four identical payment counters in a row, each staffed by an attendant in the same uniform holding the same phone with the same QR code stand on a small table. The customers are split into four short lines: a college student on a scooter, a delivery rider, an auto driver, a family in a hatchback, each paying by scanning at the same moment, shown by four small green tick bubbles appearing together. A thin bracket over the four counters shows that each one has its own complete setup: phone, QR stand, receipt pad. In the top right corner, a separate inset bubble shows a giant app icon, far bigger than the phone, failing to squeeze into a single phone screen, with four phones lined up beside it, none able to hold it, and a small red cross. Bright canopy lights against a dusky sky, efficient, everyday mood. Labels: "REPLICA" above each of the four counters, "TOO BIG" beside the inset.

key: If they move one giant crate at a time
name: ch08_dabbawala_relay_bubble
alt: A four-team dabbawala relay where one giant crate leaves three teams idle, compared with four smaller crates that keep every team busy, except at the start and end.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a horizontal line, top and bottom, each showing the same four-stage dabbawala relay from left to right: a collector at a house gate, a sorter at a station platform, a rider on a local train, and a deliverer at an office lobby, all in white kurtas and Gandhi caps. TOP panel: one enormous wooden crate of tiffins is being carried by only the sorter, straining; the collector, rider and deliverer sit idle on benches, one yawning, one reading a newspaper, one checking the time. BOTTOM panel: the load is split into four smaller crates numbered 1 to 4; the collector is picking up crate 2 while the sorter handles crate 1, then the rider carries crate 1 while the sorter takes crate 2, so every stage is busy at once, shown with staggered crates along a moving line. A thin timeline strip runs under the bottom panel with shaded triangles at its very start and very end, where only the first or last person is working. Morning light, sense of rhythm and motion in the bottom panel, sleepy stillness in the top. Labels: "ONE BIG BATCH" at the top panel's left, "MICRO-BATCHES" at the bottom panel's left, "BUBBLE" beside the shaded triangles.

key: four people each add up the runs
name: ch08_cricket_scorers_split_sum
alt: Four cricket scorers each add up a quarter of the overs at once, then call out their subtotals to each other to write the grand total.
scene: Inside a small wooden scorers' room high in a cricket stadium pavilion, with a large window overlooking the green field where a match is in progress. A long scoresheet is spread across a table and divided by thin pencil lines into four sections of overs. Four scorers sit shoulder to shoulder, each bent over one section with a calculator or pencil: a young woman in a team polo, a grey-haired man in a sweater vest, a teenage trainee with headphones around his neck, and a middle-aged man with a moustache. Each has a small subtotal written in a box in front of them. Above the table, four speech bubbles fly between the scorers, crossing each other, each carrying a short number, and all four then write the same grand total on a shared slate at the end of the table. The four sit very close together, elbows nearly touching, and a small inset on the side shows what happens if one scorer is moved to a far corner of the stadium: his shouted bubble shrinks and trails off before reaching the others. Bright afternoon sunlight from the field, focused, teamwork mood. Labels: "SPLIT" above the scoresheet sections, "COMBINE" above the crossing bubbles, "STAY CLOSE" beside the inset.

key: Running a large exam centre.
name: ch08_exam_centre_combined_parallel
alt: A large exam centre with three halls in a sequence, four invigilators splitting rows inside one hall, and a second identical centre across town.
scene: An aerial cut-away view of a school campus used as an exam centre, with a second identical campus visible small in the upper right across a city road. On the main campus, three halls are connected by a corridor, read left to right. Hall A: a desk where a staff member checks admit cards of a line of students in uniforms. Hall B: an usher shows students to numbered seats. Hall C: a large hall where four invigilators, two men and two women in formal clothes, each walk down a different set of rows handing out question papers at the same moment, the rows divided by faint coloured bands. Arrows show students flowing from Hall A to Hall B to Hall C. In the upper right, the second campus mirrors the same three halls with its own students and staff, connected to the main campus only by a road, no corridor. Inside Hall C the four invigilators exchange quick glances and short speech lines, while the two campuses have no lines between them. A small floor plan in the corner shows the number of rooms available. Clear morning light, organised, calm exam-day mood. Labels: "PIPELINE" above the corridor, "TENSOR" above Hall C, "DATA" above the second campus.

key: Rounding the prices in a kirana shop
name: ch08_kirana_rounded_prices
alt: A kirana shopkeeper's thick register of long decimal prices beside a slim notebook with rounded prices, and an inset where a very expensive item squashes small prices to zero.
scene: Inside a small neighbourhood kirana shop with sacks of rice, jars of sweets and shelves of soap behind a wooden counter. The shopkeeper, a cheerful man in his 40s with a cotton shirt, a pencil behind his ear and reading glasses on his forehead, sits at the counter with two record books open side by side. LEFT book: a fat, heavy register bulging with pages, each line filled with long prices with many decimal places written in tiny cramped digits, ink running low in his pen. RIGHT book: a slim pocket notebook where the same items have short round prices written in big clear numbers, such as "48", and plenty of empty space. A customer, a woman in a cotton saree with a cloth bag, nods happily at the slim notebook. In the upper corner, an inset bubble shows a second page where one line is for a costly item priced in lakhs and every small item beneath it, matchbox, salt, biscuits, has been flattened to a zero by a heavy stamp. Warm daylight from the shop front, friendly neighbourhood mood. Labels: "FP32" above the fat register, "INT8" above the slim notebook, "OUTLIER" beside the inset.

key: Writing distances on a road sign.
name: ch08_road_signs_fp16_bf16
alt: Two highway signs: one with many digits but few units that cannot show a huge distance, and one with all units but only a rough few digits.
scene: A long national highway stretching into the distance across plains toward hills, with two large green road signs standing side by side on poles in the foreground. A traveller couple on a motorbike, a young man in a helmet and a woman riding pillion holding a map, have stopped to read them. LEFT sign: crammed with many precise digits in small writing, but its units row only has two little slots, metres and kilometres; a long line for a faraway destination in the south runs off the edge of the sign and is cut short with a red overflow mark. RIGHT sign: shows only a short, rounded number like "about 2,800 km" in big clear letters, and its units row has many slots from millimetres up to thousands of kilometres, all lit; a tiny ant-sized distance and a huge distance are both written on it comfortably. The man points at the right sign approvingly while the woman squints at the left one. A small inset at the bottom shows many little rounding errors stacking up like a tower of coins and being caught in a wide steel box. Bright midday sun, open sky, travel mood. Labels: "FP16" above the left sign, "BF16" above the right sign.

key: A bus with 255 seat numbers.
name: ch08_bus_seats_absmax_zero_point
alt: Two city buses seen from above: one with the conductor's seat fixed in the middle and the left half empty, the other with seating shifted so every seat is used.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a horizontal line, each half showing the same long city bus from directly above with its roof cut away so every numbered seat is visible. TOP panel: the conductor, a moustached man in a khaki uniform with a ticket punch, sits at a seat marked "0" in the exact middle of the bus; all the passengers, office-goers, students, a grandmother with a bag, crowd onto seats to his right, while the entire left half of the bus is empty, rows of seats with nobody on them. BOTTOM panel: the same bus, but the zero seat marker has been moved to the very front; the first passenger sits in seat 1 and the last in seat 255 at the back, every seat filled from end to end. A small inset bubble at the side shows a third tiny bus where one giant passenger takes up a huge stretch of seats, and all the normal-sized passengers are squeezed together onto the same single seat. Bright midday light, slightly comic mood. Labels: "ABSMAX" at the left of the top panel, "ZERO-POINT" at the left of the bottom panel, "OUTLIER" beside the inset.

key: Packing sarees for a trip.
name: ch08_saree_pouches_gguf
alt: Sarees folded into small pouches each sized to its biggest saree, the pouches packed into labelled bags inside a suitcase with a packing list, carried in a small car.
scene: A bedroom floor before a family trip, viewed from slightly above. A woman in her 40s in a cotton salwar suit kneels beside an open suitcase, carefully folding colourful silk and cotton sarees. In front of her, sarees are grouped into small zip pouches; each pouch has a tiny tag, and a measuring tape lies beside the pouch showing it was folded to fit its biggest saree, while a second pouch has two tags, biggest and smallest, so the folds sit snugly. Nearby, eight pouches are packed together inside a larger cloth bag with one compact label strip listing each pouch's size. In the open suitcase, several of these bags fit neatly, and on the inside of the lid a handwritten packing list is taped. On the right side, through an open door, a small hatchback car waits in the driveway, its boot open, and her teenage son lifts the closed suitcase into it with ease. Soft morning light through lace curtains, homely and organised mood. Labels: "BLOCKS" above the pouches, "K-QUANTS" above the larger bag, "GGUF" above the suitcase lid.

key: Rounding the bill at a group dinner.
name: ch08_dinner_bill_gptq
alt: Friends at a dinner table split the bill: rounding each share leaves the total short, while passing each rounding difference to the next person keeps the total right.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same restaurant table after a group dinner, five friends in their 20s, a mix of men and women in casual clothes, with empty plates and a bill folder in the centre. LEFT panel: each friend has a slip with a neatly rounded share and puts cash on the table, but a waiter holding the bill looks unhappy, and a small red gap bar shows the collected money falling short. RIGHT panel: the friends sit in a row and pass a small notepad from one to the next; the first friend rounds her share and writes the leftover amount on the notepad with a curved arrow handing it to the next friend, who adjusts his share, and so on down the line; at the end the waiter smiles and gives a thumbs-up, the green bar full. In the right panel, one friend who ordered a large biryani and kebabs rounds carefully with a fine pen, while another who only had chai rounds roughly with a broad marker, shown by different pen tips. Warm restaurant lighting, cheerful mood. Labels: "NAIVE" above the left panel, "GPTQ" above the right panel, "EXL2" near the two different pens.

key: AWQ is a tailor who measures where
name: ch08_tailor_awq_cabin_bag
alt: A tailor reinforces the seams where a kurta stretches most when worn, and a traveller squeezes a big wardrobe into a tiny cabin bag that still holds more outfits than a loosely packed small one.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a small tailoring shop with a sewing machine, bolts of cloth and a mirror. An elderly tailor in his 60s with a measuring tape around his neck and spectacles watches a young man in a new kurta raise his arms and bend; the cloth at the shoulders and elbows glows with small stretch lines, and the tailor marks those exact spots with chalk and reinforces them with tight stitches, ignoring a thick but unstressed hem at the bottom. A thin arrow points from the stretch lines to the chalk marks. RIGHT panel: an airport check-in queue; a woman traveller in her 30s with a backpack kneels and presses down on a tiny cabin suitcase packed extremely tight with a big wardrobe's worth of outfits, the lid barely closing; beside her, a second traveller carries an equally small bag packed loosely with only two outfits. A small comparison bubble above them shows more outfit icons coming out of the tightly packed bag. Warm workshop light on the left, bright airport light on the right, practical and lightly humorous mood. Labels: "AWQ" above the left panel, "1-2 BIT" above the right panel.

key: A railway enquiry counter.
name: ch09_enquiry_counter_status_board
alt: Back-office staff update a train-status board while a clerk at the enquiry window only reads the board to answer passengers.
scene: A cut-away view of a railway station enquiry office, split by a wall into a back room and a front window. LEFT, the back room: two back-office staff, a woman in a blue railway uniform and a young man with a headset, climb a small ladder and slide new train-status tiles into a large board on the dividing wall, a wall clock and a printed schedule beside them, with a small circular arrow showing they do this every few minutes. RIGHT, the front: a clerk in his 40s with a moustache and spectacles sits behind a glass window with a round speaking hole, turned sideways to read the very same board through a hatch, and answers a queue of passengers outside: a family with suitcases, a student with a backpack, an elderly man with a walking stick. He never touches the board; a thin dotted line shows his eyes going from the board to the passengers. The two rooms have separate doors and separate light switches, and a small sign on the back-room door reads "STAFF ONLY". In a tiny inset, a train just arriving on a platform is not yet on the board, and a puzzled passenger asks about it. Bright station lighting, busy but orderly mood. Labels: "FEATURE PIPELINE" above the back room, "RETRIEVAL" above the clerk's window.

key: Asking a librarian for help with a
name: ch09_librarian_full_retrieval
alt: A librarian rephrases a student's request three ways, searches three shelves with an author filter, removes duplicate books, skims each against the question and hands over the best three.
scene: A wide view of an old public library with tall wooden shelves, ladders and green reading lamps, laid out as a left-to-right journey. FAR LEFT: a schoolboy of about 13 in uniform with a notebook asks a kind librarian in her 50s, cotton saree and spectacles on a chain, for help; three speech bubbles above her show the request rephrased three different ways with small train and steam-engine icons. CENTRE: the librarian, with an author's name card clipped to her cardigan as a filter, pulls books from three different shelves at once, with three thin arrows from the shelves to a book trolley. CENTRE-RIGHT: on the trolley a pile of books, two of them identical copies; she sets the duplicate aside on a separate small stack. RIGHT: at a reading table she opens each book, holding the boy's question slip beside it and skimming, three books given green ribbons and the rest pushed away. FAR RIGHT: the boy at a desk writes his essay with the three chosen books open in front of him. Soft afternoon light through high windows, dust in the air, helpful and calm mood. Labels: "EXPAND" above the speech bubbles, "FILTER" by the name card, "RERANK" above the reading table.

key: A dabbawala route. Every dabbawala
name: ch09_dabbawala_empty_tiffin_practice
alt: Dabbawalas hand tiffins over at fixed points along a route, and in a practice run they carry empty tiffins to test the route without real food.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, showing the same dabbawala route from a housing society gate to a railway platform to an office lobby, with fixed handover points marked by painted circles on the ground. LEFT panel: real lunch day; at each painted circle one dabbawala in a white kurta and Gandhi cap hands a tiffin to the next with both hands, and two tiffin icons above show one cooked at home by a grandmother in an apron and one bought from a roadside stall; the next dabbawala treats them the same. RIGHT panel: a practice morning; the same dabbawalas pass along shiny steel tiffins that are clearly empty, shown with their lids open and nothing inside, a trainee in a new cap timing the run with a stopwatch, the route working smoothly. In a small inset bubble on the right, a question mark hovers over a closed tiffin tipped sideways, since nobody can tell whether real dal would have spilled. Bright morning light, organised and cheerful mood. Labels: "INTERFACE" above the painted handover circles, "MOCK" above the right panel.

key: A courier parcel. The contents
name: ch09_courier_parcel_airway_bill
alt: A courier parcel is opened and repacked with the same airway bill stuck on it, then gets a sorting barcode so machines can route it.
scene: A courier sorting hub seen in a wide left-to-right sequence along a work table and a conveyor belt. LEFT: a cardboard parcel with a printed airway bill stuck on its side, showing an id number, a sender name and a short note. CENTRE-LEFT: a packer in her 30s, company polo shirt and cap, opens the box, takes out the old contents and places new, neatly wrapped contents inside, while the same airway bill stays on the outside, highlighted with a soft glow; a curved arrow shows old contents leaving and new ones entering. CENTRE-RIGHT: a young worker with a hand-held printer sticks a fresh barcode sticker next to the airway bill. RIGHT: the parcel rides the conveyor into a sorting machine with scanners and coloured chutes, a red laser line reading the barcode and a diverter arm pushing the parcel into the correct chute. In the background, shelves of parcels and a big hanging clock. A small inset bubble near the packer shows two boxes side by side with matching airway bills, one labelled old and one new, to hint they are different objects with the same labels. Bright warehouse lighting, efficient mood. Labels: "REPACK" above the packer, "EMBEDDING" beside the barcode, "ROUTE" above the machine.

key: Before a chartered accountant files
name: ch09_ca_junior_clerk_pan
alt: A junior clerk tidies a client's messy request into standard sections and notes the PAN so only that client's documents reach the expensive chartered accountant.
scene: A small chartered accountant's office with steel almirahs full of files, a calendar on the wall and a ceiling fan, shown left to right. LEFT: a worried shopkeeper in his 50s in a kurta dumps a pile of crumpled bills, receipts and handwritten notes on the front desk. CENTRE: a quick junior clerk in his early 20s with a neat side parting and a shirt with rolled sleeves sorts the mess into a clean form with standard sections drawn as coloured blocks, and copies one card into a box at the top: a PAN card, shown only as a small card with an id photo and a blank number area. A thin arrow goes from that box to a tall cabinet behind him, where only one drawer with the matching card slides open and every other drawer stays shut. RIGHT: in a glass cabin, the senior chartered accountant, a woman in her 50s with spectacles and a crisp saree, receives the tidy form and the single file, ready to work; a small price-tag icon above her shows she is the expensive expert, while a tiny stopwatch over the clerk shows his work takes only a minute. Warm office light, practical mood. Labels: "REWRITE" above the clerk's form, "FILTER" beside the opened drawer, "EXPERT" above the accountant.

key: A teacher asks a student to
name: ch09_teacher_three_ways_separator
alt: A teacher asks a student to restate a question three ways, one per line with a separator between them, on a blackboard where the number three is fixed and the question changes each period.
scene: A bright school classroom with wooden benches, a ceiling fan and a big green blackboard. At the front stands a teacher in her 40s in a printed cotton saree, holding a piece of chalk and a timetable card. On the blackboard, written before class in permanent paint at the top corner, is a fixed instruction box with the number "3" circled; below it, freshly written in chalk, is today's question, with a small eraser sitting next to it to show it changes every period. A student of about 14, in a white shirt and tie, stands at the board writing three versions of the question on three separate lines, with a row of hash symbols "###" between each line like dividers. A thin arrow from the teacher's own question to the first line shows her words count as version one. On the side, a small inset bubble shows a second, careless student's notebook where the three versions run together on one line without any separators, and the teacher's red pen circles it with a question mark. Morning sunlight through tall windows, chalk dust in the air, orderly classroom mood. Labels: "PARTIAL" beside the fixed box, "INPUT" beside the chalk question, "SEPARATOR" beside the hash row.

key: On a matrimonial site you type
name: ch09_matrimonial_hard_filters
alt: A matrimonial search where a pure vibe match suggests a cricket-loving engineer from the wrong city, while hard filters for city and language narrow the profiles first.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. On the far left edge, a mother in her 50s in a salwar suit sits on a sofa with a tablet, her son in his late 20s leaning over her shoulder, both looking at the screen; their search request floats above as a speech bubble with small icons for an engineer's hard hat, a city landmark, a language script and a cricket bat. LEFT panel: a wall of profile cards ranked only by similarity; the top card shows a smiling engineer holding a cricket bat but standing in front of a different city's skyline, with a red mismatch mark on the city icon, and the mother frowns. RIGHT panel: two sieves stacked one above the other; the first sieve only lets through cards with the right city pin, the second only cards with the right language badge; below the sieves, a smaller set of cards is then ranked by the cricket and engineer icons, and the top card shows the right city and language; the mother and son smile and point. Warm living-room lamplight, gently humorous family mood. Labels: "VIBE ONLY" above the left panel, "FILTER FIRST" above the right panel.

key: Without a filter the assistant brings
name: ch09_java_bookshop_filter
alt: A bookshop assistant brings both a programming book and an island travel guide with the same word on the cover, until a computer-section filter sends her straight to the right shelves.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in a big multi-floor bookshop with signboards for sections. LEFT panel: a young software developer in his 20s with a laptop bag waits at the counter while a shop assistant in her 20s, wearing a store apron, comes back from a long walk across the whole shop carrying a mixed armful: a thick programming book with a coffee cup on the cover and a travel guide with a tropical island and volcano on its cover; both covers show the same single word "JAVA" in big letters. The developer looks puzzled; dotted footprints show her winding route through cooking, travel, fiction and computer sections. RIGHT panel: the developer points at a hanging sign over one aisle reading "COMPUTERS"; the assistant walks straight there along a short direct path, checks only three shelves, and returns with three programming books, all fitting. In a small inset in the corner, one excellent programming book sits misplaced on a general shelf, out of the path, with a faint shadow over it. Bright bookshop lighting, light humorous mood. Labels: "NO FILTER" above the left panel, "FILTERED" above the right panel.

key: A singleton is the one pressure cooker
name: ch09_shared_pressure_cooker
alt: In a joint-family kitchen, everyone shares one pressure cooker, and a recipe card that just says three whistles works for a new electric cooker too.
scene: A large joint-family kitchen with steel utensils on wall racks, a gas stove and a window with curtains, seen in a warm medium shot. On the stove sits one single pressure cooker, its whistle puffing steam. Around it, four family members wait their turn with ingredients: a grandmother in a white saree with a bowl of dal, a daughter-in-law in a printed nightie with soaked rajma, a teenage son with rice, and an uncle with chana, all forming a small line instead of each holding their own cooker; a crossed-out thought bubble above them shows four separate cookers crowding the stove. Pinned on the wall next to the stove is a simple recipe card with a cooker icon and three whistle symbols. In the right foreground, a shiny new electric pressure cooker sits in a box on the counter, and a dotted arrow shows the same recipe card applying to it unchanged. A small inset near the line shows two people trying to cook at the same time and bumping elbows, with a little warning mark. Morning sunlight, homely, slightly humorous mood. Labels: "SINGLETON" above the cooker on the stove, "WRAPPER" beside the recipe card.

key: Building a new metro line: tracks
name: ch09_metro_line_waiting_train
alt: A new metro line with finished tracks, stations and signals tested section by section, waiting for the train cars to arrive before passengers can ride end to end.
scene: A wide panoramic view of a new elevated metro line running across a city from left to right, with apartment blocks and a sunset sky behind. On the left, workers in orange vests and hard hats test a finished section of track with a hand trolley and a measuring device. In the middle, a gleaming new station with ticket gates and a platform, where an engineer in her 30s with a clipboard checks the screen-door controls. On the right, a signalling cabin where a technician in a helmet flips switches and green signal lights glow along the track. Every section has a small green tick floating above it. But the platform is empty of trains and a few curious residents look down the line expectantly; far in the distance, on a highway, a large trailer truck slowly brings the first gleaming train car, wrapped in plastic, toward the depot. On the near track, a small yellow test engine with one cabin runs a trial along a short section. Golden evening light, sense of anticipation. Labels: "READY" above the tested sections, "MODEL" above the train car on the truck.

key: A thali with three katoris
name: ch09_thali_three_katoris
alt: A steel thali with three katoris for dal, sabzi and raita, one scoop each, and a second thali with an empty raita katori because the kitchen ran out.
scene: A close-up, top-down view of two shiny steel thalis on a wooden dining table in a homely restaurant. LEFT thali: three small katoris arranged in a curve, one with yellow dal, one with green sabzi, one with white raita, each holding exactly one ladle-sized scoop; rotis and rice fill the rest of the plate, and a server's hand with a steel ladle hovers above, showing the rule of one scoop per katori. RIGHT thali: the same layout, but the raita katori sits empty and clean; behind the table, the server, a young man with a striped apron and a kind smile, holds up an empty raita bucket with an apologetic shrug, while the customer, a woman in her 30s with a dupatta, nods happily at a still complete meal. A small sign on the wall reads "MAX 1" with a ladle icon. In a tiny inset in the corner, a third thali shows the dal katori overflowing with dal from an extra-good batch that has no space to go, hinting at a fixed split's limits. Warm overhead light, comfortable lunchtime mood. Labels: "K PER CATEGORY" above the left thali, "SHORT BUT VALID" above the right thali.

key: Three friends each bring their shortlist
name: ch09_three_friends_restaurant_lists
alt: Three friends combine their restaurant shortlists, strike out repeats, and a friend who knows everyone's taste ranks the rest to pick three to book.
scene: A cosy café table in the evening seen from slightly above, four friends in their 20s gathered around it. Three of them each lay down a handwritten list on a small paper card: a woman in a denim jacket, a man in a kurta, and a man with a cap. In the centre, the lists are drawn merging into one long combined paper scroll, with arrows from each card flowing into it. On the scroll, one restaurant name that appears on two lists is struck out once with a pen, with a small tally of two dots beside it that is then erased, hinting the vote count is lost. The fourth friend, a confident young woman with glasses who knows everyone's taste, holds a pen and numbers the remaining places in order, with tiny icons of each friend's favourite food floating above her head. On the right side of the table, the top three choices are circled and she is booking them on her phone. Warm string lights, coffee cups, cheerful planning mood. Labels: "MERGE" above the scroll, "DEDUPE" beside the struck-out name, "RERANK" above the friend with the pen.

key: A wedding planner (ContextRetriever)
name: ch09_wedding_planner_retriever
alt: A wedding planner checks the guest list, sends three assistants to three markets at once, merges their shopping, removes duplicates and has the head cook pick the best.
scene: A busy wedding house courtyard decorated with marigold garlands, seen from slightly above, with a central figure and three branching paths. CENTRE: a composed wedding planner in her 30s in a smart kurta with a headset and clipboard checks a guest list for a family name highlighted with a marker. From her, three dotted paths run out at the same time to three small market scenes at the top of the image: a vegetable market, a flower market and a sweets market, each with one young assistant carrying a shopping bag; a small clock above all three shows the same time. The paths return to a big table in the lower right where all the shopping is piled up, two identical boxes of sweets placed side by side with one pushed aside into a reject crate. At the end of the table, the head cook, a burly man in his 50s with an apron, tastes and selects the best items into a final basket. In a tiny inset, all three assistants crowd into the same single packed market, bumping into each other. Bright festive daylight, energetic mood. Labels: "SELF-QUERY" by the guest list, "PARALLEL" above the three markets, "RERANK" above the head cook.

key: A good news anchor reads the story
name: ch09_news_anchor_source_credit
alt: A TV news anchor reads a story and credits the news agency, while a viewer at home follows the credit line to check the original report.
scene: A split view: on the left two thirds, a television news studio; on the right third, a family living room. In the studio, a professional news anchor in her 40s in a crisp blazer sits at a glossy desk with a teleprompter in front of her, reading a story; beneath her on the screen a lower-third strip shows the story and a small credit tag with a wire icon, and thin threads run from that credit tag back to a stack of three printed wire reports on a side desk behind the camera, each report with a different coloured clip. In the living room, a retired man in a sleeveless sweater sits on a sofa with a cup of tea and taps a link on his phone, an arrow from his phone leading back to the matching wire report in the studio. A small inset bubble near the anchor shows a sentence on the teleprompter connected by a thread to the wrong coloured report, a tiny warning sign beside it. Bright studio lights on the left, warm lamp light on the right, trustworthy and calm mood. Labels: "SOURCE" beside the credit tag, "CHECK" above the viewer.

key: A newspaper columnist with a research
name: ch09_columnist_clippings_template
alt: A research assistant drops three clippings on a columnist's desk under an editor's note, and the columnist writes the column from them.
scene: A newspaper columnist's office with wooden bookshelves, a window over the city and a desk lamp, in a medium shot. On the left, a young research assistant in his 20s with a lanyard and a satchel sets three newspaper clippings on the desk, each clipping slightly overlapping the next, with a dotted line tracing back to a large archive cabinet behind him. On top of the clippings sits a pinned editor's note card with a short instruction and an arrow pointing down at the clippings. In the centre, the columnist, a thoughtful woman in her 50s with silver-streaked hair, reading glasses and a shawl, types on a typewriter, her eyes moving between the clippings and the page. On the right edge, a small calendar marked slow day shows an alternative scene in an inset bubble: the same columnist writing from memory with no clippings, a cloud of her own thoughts above her. Also on the right, the assistant is seen in a second tiny vignette handing clippings to another writer at the next desk. Warm afternoon light, quiet professional mood. Labels: "RETRIEVER" above the assistant, "TEMPLATE" beside the editor's note, "LLM" above the columnist.

key: The reception desk at a big government
name: ch09_hospital_reception_router
alt: A hospital receptionist reads a patient's slip and sends them to one or two of three outpatient departments instead of all three.
scene: The crowded ground floor of a large government hospital with a high ceiling, tiled floors and hanging signboards, seen in a wide shot. In the centre is a reception counter where a calm receptionist in her 40s, in a white coat over a saree with a pen in hand, reads a paper slip handed in by a patient, an elderly farmer in a dhoti and turban with a cloth bag. Behind her, three corridors branch off to three outpatient departments, each with a small icon sign: a stethoscope, a heart and a bone. Bold arrows from the counter lead the farmer only toward the heart corridor, and a second, lighter arrow toward the general corridor, while the bone corridor has no arrow and its queue is short. In a contrast inset bubble in the corner, a confused patient wanders down all three corridors in turn, worn out. In another tiny inset, a patient sent to the wrong corridor stands at a door while the right department far away has a doctor waiting. Bright fluorescent light, busy but efficient mood. Labels: "ROUTER" above the reception counter, "COLLECTIONS" above the three corridors.

key: Hybrid search lets one search box
name: ch09_train_search_hybrid
alt: At a railway enquiry kiosk, one traveller types an exact train number while another types a description, and one search box serves both.
scene: A modern railway station concourse with a large departure board, and a self-service kiosk with a big touch screen in the centre of the frame. LEFT: a regular commuter in his 30s in a formal shirt and lanyard confidently taps in an exact five-digit train number, shown as big digits on the screen with a sharp target icon, and gets a single precise result. RIGHT: a first-time traveller, a young woman from a village with a large suitcase and a dupatta over her head, describes what she needs in a speech bubble with icons of a moon, a sleeping berth and two city skylines, and the screen shows a list of matching overnight trains with a soft heart icon for meaning. Both people are using the same single search box at the top of the kiosk, with two arrows, one sharp and one wavy, merging into it. Above the kiosk, a small balance scale in an inset shows marks out of 100 on one pan and grades out of 10 on the other, tipped badly until a converter gear evens them. Bright station lighting, helpful mood. Labels: "KEYWORD" above the commuter, "MEANING" above the traveller, "HYBRID" above the search box.

key: Picking a restaurant on a food app.
name: ch09_food_app_multi_index
alt: A man picks dinner on a food app where dish, delivery area and opening date are weighed together on one scale instead of applied one after another.
scene: A small apartment living room at night; a young man in his 20s in shorts and a T-shirt sits cross-legged on a bean bag holding his phone, hungry, a cat curled next to him. Above him floats a large enlarged phone screen showing restaurant cards. On the left of the screen, a single search chip shows a biryani pot icon. On the right, three chips feed into a big balance-like mixing bowl: a biryani pot icon, a scooter-on-map icon for delivers to my area, and a new-shop ribbon icon for opened recently, each pouring a different coloured stream into the bowl, with small sliders below each stream showing their weight. Out of the bottom of the bowl comes one single ranked list of restaurant cards. In a small inset at the corner, a slider for recent is pushed all the way up, and a beloved old restaurant card with a dusty look slides off the bottom of the list. Warm lamp light mixed with phone glow, cosy late-night mood. Labels: "CONTENT" by the biryani chip, "MULTI-INDEX" above the mixing bowl, "WEIGHTS" by the sliders.

key: A brilliant home cook (the trained
name: ch10_home_cook_opens_tiffin_service
alt: A talented home cook standing in her kitchen considers three ways to open a tiffin service: cook to order, take orders for later, or pack dabbas in bulk each morning.
scene: A home kitchen in a neighbourhood building, shown in a medium-wide shot. In the centre stands a talented home cook in her 40s, a cotton saree tucked at the waist, flour on her hands, beside a stove with fragrant pots; a small trophy and a framed cooking-contest certificate hang on the wall behind her, but her front door is still closed and neighbours outside cannot reach her food. Above her head three thought bubbles branch out like options. FIRST bubble: a customer standing at her kitchen window waiting while she cooks one plate fresh. SECOND bubble: a notepad of orders and a delivery boy on a scooter leaving later with packed boxes. THIRD bubble: a neat stack of steel dabbas packed early in the morning on a table by the door, with people picking them up. Below the bubbles, a second row of two small sketches: one big kitchen where she does everything, and one where a separate small stove is set aside just for an expensive dish. In the far corner, a small inset shows her recipe being copied onto many identical kitchen counters at once. Warm morning light, hopeful mood. Labels: "REAL-TIME", "ASYNC" and "BATCH" under the three thought bubbles in that order.

key: A UPI payment check (a few fields
name: ch10_upi_check_vs_wedding_speech
alt: A shopkeeper's quick phone payment check finishes in a blink, while a man slowly writes a long wedding speech from a thick folder of notes about the couple.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a small paan and cigarette shop at a street corner; a college student in a T-shirt scans a QR code on the counter with her phone, and the shopkeeper's phone speaker instantly chirps with a green tick bubble; a stopwatch icon above shows a tiny fraction of a second; the request is shown as a slim card with only three short fields. RIGHT panel: a cramped study room at night; the bride's elder brother, a man in his 30s in a vest and pyjamas, sits at a desk buried under a thick folder of photos, family stories and notes about the couple, writing a very long speech that unrolls off the desk onto the floor like a scroll; crumpled drafts surround him and a wall clock shows hours passing; a stopwatch icon above him has its hand spun around many times. Between the two panels, a small arrow shows both arriving at the same kind of counter labelled request, to stress they look alike from outside. Bright daylight on the left, dim lamp light on the right, gently comic mood. Labels: "SMALL IN, SMALL OUT" above the left panel, "LONG IN, LONG OUT" above the right panel.

key: Renting a tempo for a shop
name: ch10_tempo_rental_sizing
alt: A shop owner's big rented truck drives half-empty on a normal day, while a tiny tempo cannot keep up with the parcels on a festival day.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves outside the same small home-appliances shop with a painted signboard. LEFT panel: an ordinary weekday; a huge rented truck is parked outside with its back doors open, and inside there are just three small boxes in a large empty cargo bed; the shop owner, a man in his 40s with a moustache and a calculator, frowns at a bill showing a high cost per parcel, while the driver leans against the cab looking bored. RIGHT panel: a festival day with marigold strings and diyas on the shop; a tiny three-wheeler tempo is overloaded with boxes tied with rope, tilting to one side, and a long pile of parcels still waits on the pavement while customers wait impatiently with receipts; the same owner wipes sweat off his forehead. In the top corner a small inset shows a rental desk where trucks of different sizes can be picked up and returned by the minute, with a clock beside it. Daylight on the left, festive evening glow on the right, light humorous mood. Labels: "TOO BIG" above the left panel, "TOO SMALL" above the right panel.

key: Calling a customer-care line and staying
name: ch10_on_hold_rest_vs_grpc
alt: A man waits on hold for a customer-care answer; nearby, two bank branches exchange short coded messages using a shared codebook instead of plain sentences.
scene: A split illustration with a top strip and a bottom strip. TOP strip: a man in his 30s in office clothes sits on his sofa holding a phone to his ear, on hold, a curly line of hold music notes flowing from the phone; he cannot do anything else, a cup of tea going cold in front of him and his laptop closed, and a small clock shows minutes passing until a smiling agent's face finally appears in a bubble with the answer. BOTTOM strip, split in two: on the left, two clerks at two desks talk across a gap in long, full sentences shown as wide speech bubbles with many words, any passer-by able to follow; on the right, two bank branch clerks, one in each branch building, send short coded slips through a pneumatic tube, each slip holding just a few symbols, and both clerks hold identical thick codebooks open on their desks to decode them; their slips are visibly smaller and fly faster. Office daylight, calm and practical mood. Labels: "SYNC" above the top strip, "REST" above the long-sentence clerks, "GRPC" above the codebook branches.

key: Hiring a heart surgeon who also does
name: ch10_surgeon_doing_billing
alt: A heart surgeon in scrubs sits at a hospital billing counter filling forms while the operating theatre behind him stands idle and a meter of his fees keeps running.
scene: A hospital ground floor with a reception and billing counter in the foreground and a glass wall behind it revealing a modern operating theatre. At the counter sits a heart surgeon in his 50s, still in green scrubs, cap and a stethoscope around his neck, wearily stamping and filling patient forms, a tall stack of paperwork beside him and a queue of patients with files waiting. Behind the glass, the operating theatre is fully equipped with bright lights, monitors and a ready table, but empty and idle, with a nurse looking at her watch. Above the surgeon's head floats a large taxi-style meter with rupee coins pouring out of it, ticking up while he fills forms. To the right, a smiling young receptionist in a hospital uniform stands at the side of the counter with nothing to do, holding a pen, as if ready to take over. On the wall clock above the counter the minute hand has swept a long arc, and a patient on a trolley waits by the theatre door with a worried relative holding her hand. Even, slightly cold hospital lighting, ironic, lightly humorous mood. Labels: "EXPENSIVE" above the meter, "IDLE" above the empty theatre.

key: Building a house with the plumbing in
name: ch10_labelled_pipes_house
alt: A house wall with clearly labelled pipes behind removable panels, where a plumber easily adds a bathroom, compared with pipes buried in concrete needing demolition.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, each half showing a cross-section of the same two-storey house wall. LEFT panel: pipes are buried deep inside solid concrete walls, invisible; a labourer in a vest swings a sledgehammer, breaking a large hole to find the right pipe, dust and rubble everywhere, and the homeowner in a kurta holds his head in dismay. RIGHT panel: the same wall fitted with neat removable panels; one panel is lifted off to show tidy colour-coded pipes, each with a clear tag, running in straight lines; a cheerful plumber in a cap and overalls connects one new pipe to a fresh bathroom block being added beside the house with just a wrench, while the homeowner sips tea calmly nearby. A thin arrow from the new bathroom block to the labelled pipe shows how simple the joint is. In the right panel, a small open tool bag holds only a wrench and a roll of tape, while on the left a hired jackhammer and a pile of broken bricks fill the courtyard. Bright daylight, clean and practical mood on the right, chaotic on the left. Labels: "TANGLED" above the left panel, "MODULAR" above the right panel.

key: A food court. The endpoint is the
name: ch10_food_court_endpoint
alt: A food court counter window serving customers, backed by recipe books and rented kitchen equipment, with arrangements assigning each recipe to specific stoves and cooks.
scene: A bright mall food court in a wide shot. In the foreground, a single stall with one serving window where a short queue of customers waits: a mother and child, an office worker, two college friends. Above the window hangs a counter sign. Behind the window, the kitchen is shown in cut-away. On a shelf sit two recipe books, one with a dosa icon and one with a noodle icon. Rented kitchen equipment fills the space: four stoves, a fryer and a hood, each with a small rental tag. Two arrangement cards are pinned on a board: the first card links the dosa recipe book with lines to two specific stoves and two cooks in caps; the second card links the noodle recipe book to the other two stoves and one cook. A thin arrow from the serving window leads to the board, showing the order is routed by the card's name rather than by what the customer says. Warm mall lighting, lively, organised mood. Labels: "ENDPOINT" above the serving window, "MODEL" beside the recipe books, "COMPONENT" above the arrangement cards.

key: Training is a cricket net session
name: ch10_nets_vs_match_skew
alt: A batsman practises at crowded nets with bowling machines on a matting pitch, then struggles in a real match on a turf pitch.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same young batsman in his early 20s in both halves, white kit and helmet. LEFT panel: a busy net session; several bowling machines fire balls in sequence, two coaches with clipboards watch, a pile of hundreds of balls sits in buckets, and a wall clock shows no rush; the pitch under his feet is a green rubber matting strip with a visible seam. The batsman calmly drives balls one after another, relaxed. RIGHT panel: a packed stadium during a real match; one bowler charges in, the ball is a blur, and the scoreboard shows the match situation; under the batsman's feet is a natural brown turf pitch with cracks. He mistimes the shot, the ball spinning off the edge, his face startled. A thin arrow from the matting in the left panel to the turf in the right panel carries a small not-equal sign. Soft morning light on the nets, bright floodlights in the stadium, tense mood on the right. Labels: "TRAINING" above the left panel, "INFERENCE" above the right panel, "SKEW" beside the not-equal sign.

key: A restaurant can have the best chef
name: ch10_locked_door_best_chef
alt: A famous chef cooks beautifully inside a locked restaurant while hungry customers turn away to a busy dhaba next door.
scene: A street view at lunchtime with two eateries side by side. LEFT: an elegant restaurant with a glass front; inside, a celebrated chef in his 40s in a tall white hat plates a beautiful dish with care, steam and sparkles above it; but the front door has a heavy padlock and chain, and the lone waiter inside dozes on a chair with an order pad on his lap, a cobweb on the order bell. Outside its door, a family and two office workers rattle the handle, frustrated, one checking her watch. RIGHT: a simple roadside dhaba with plastic chairs and an open front, a waiter in a vest briskly carrying steaming plates to tables, the cook waving customers in; the same family is now shown walking over and taking seats, with a curved arrow showing their path from the locked door to the dhaba. A second waiter at the dhaba scribbles orders quickly on a pad and shouts them to the kitchen, and a hand-painted board outside promises quick service. On the restaurant's glass, a small sign shows opening hours that nobody can see past the chain. Bright noon sunlight, light ironic mood. Labels: "MODEL" above the chef, "DEPLOYMENT" beside the padlocked door.

key: An apartment society: the secretary
name: ch10_society_keys_iam
alt: An apartment society secretary uses a master key to cut a key that opens only the pump room for a plumber, while the lift carries its own maintenance badge.
scene: The ground floor of an apartment building, shown in cut-away with a lobby, a pump room door and a lift. LEFT: the society secretary, a retired gentleman in his 60s in a sleeveless sweater and spectacles, holds a big golden master key on a ring at a small key-cutting stand, where a locksmith cuts a small silver copy. CENTRE: a young plumber in overalls with a toolbag holds the new silver key; a dotted arrow shows it fits only the door marked with a water-pump icon, while the doors to the terrace, the office and the flats show small red locks that it does not open. RIGHT: the lift's open doors reveal a maintenance badge clipped inside the car, and a dotted arrow from the badge leads only to the lift shaft and a logbook on a shelf, nowhere else; a lift technician's tablet glows with the badge's limited access. In a small corner inset, a key with a tiny timer on it fades out after a while. Clean daylight in the lobby, orderly, secure mood. Labels: "ADMIN" above the master key, "IAM USER" beside the plumber, "EXECUTION ROLE" beside the lift badge.

key: Booking a wedding hall through a planner
name: ch10_planner_venue_manager
alt: A wedding planner calls a venue manager, who first checks the booking register before setting up the hall, and the same script works with another city's venue manager.
scene: A three-part composition read left to right. LEFT: a calm wedding planner in her 30s in a smart kurta and headset sits at a desk with a simple step-by-step script card, making a phone call. CENTRE: in a banquet hall office, a venue manager in his 40s in a suit answers the call, and first opens a thick booking register on his desk, running his finger down a page to check if the hall is already booked under the family's name; a small magnifying-glass icon hovers over the name. RIGHT: only after the check, staff in uniforms set up chairs, a mandap and flower decorations in a grand hall. Beneath the centre scene, a second smaller venue manager from another city, in a different coloured suit, is shown as a swappable card, with a curved arrow showing he can replace the first, while the planner's script card on the left stays exactly the same. In a tiny inset, the register reveals an existing booking and a red stop sign pops up instead of setup. Warm interior lighting, efficient professional mood. Labels: "STRATEGY" above the planner, "DEPLOYMENT SERVICE" above the venue manager, "RESOURCE MANAGER" beside the register.

key: Sending a courier: the executor writes
name: ch10_courier_letter_envelope
alt: One clerk writes a letter on a fixed template, another puts it in the right envelope with the address label and hands it to a courier company counter.
scene: A small office mail room shown as a left-to-right line of three stations. LEFT: a clerk in her 30s in a printed kurta writes a letter on a pre-printed template sheet with fixed boxes, filling in only the blanks, a stack of identical templates beside her. CENTRE: a second clerk, a young man in a shirt and tie, folds the letter into an envelope and sticks on an address label and a small content-type tag, checking a list on the wall to choose the right envelope. RIGHT: a courier company counter with a uniformed agent who accepts the sealed envelope, a parcel scale and a delivery van visible through a door. The envelope clerk is waiting at the counter with a clock above him, refusing to move until the agent returns a receipt. In a small inset, a second courier company's counter of a different colour is swapped in, and only the envelope clerk's labels change while the letter writer keeps working. Bright office daylight, orderly mood. Labels: "EXECUTOR" above the letter writer, "CLIENT" above the envelope clerk, "COURIER" above the counter.

key: front desk: it takes your request
name: ch10_travel_desk_specialist
alt: At a travel agency front desk, an agent takes a printed form, checks files, then phones an expensive specialist; when the line is dead she tells the customer to try later.
scene: A small travel agency with posters of mountains and beaches on the walls. In the foreground, a front-desk agent in her 20s with a neat bun and a name badge sits behind a counter. A customer, a middle-aged man in a checked shirt with a rolled umbrella, has just handed her a printed request form with tidy boxes. She looks things up in a filing cabinet drawer and on her computer, and calls an airline on a desk phone. To the right, through a glass partition, a senior travel specialist in a separate expensive-looking cabin, wearing a headset and surrounded by maps and screens, is connected by a long phone cord from the agent's second phone, drawn as a bold line. A small inset bubble near the cord shows the cord cut with a spark, and the agent politely holding up a small sign to the customer reading "TRY LATER" instead of waiting forever. On the agent's desk sits a small tray of stamped forms already handled, a tiny globe and a table calendar, and the customer leans forward with polite impatience. Bright office light, practical mood.
