Labels: "FORM" on the customer's sheet, "GPU SERVICE" above the specialist's cabin.

key: may run with between 1 and 20 coaches
name: ch10_train_coach_range
alt: A railway officer registers that a train may run with between one and twenty coaches, while a separate rule book on when to add coaches sits apart.
scene: A railway yard at dawn with a long track curving away. On the track, a locomotive is coupled to just one passenger coach, and a long row of nineteen spare coaches waits on a siding beside it, shown in faded outline as possible additions. In the foreground, a railway officer in his 50s in a white uniform with a cap and moustache stands at a small table in the open, stamping a registration certificate that shows a short range bar from 1 to 20 with a coach icon at each end. A thin bracket over the train and siding matches the range on the certificate. To the right, on a separate desk under a tin shed, a second, closed rule book with a clock and a crowd icon on its cover sits untouched, with a dashed line separating it from the certificate to show it is a different document. A signal post with a green light stands beside the locomotive, and a couple of yard workers in orange vests wait near the siding with coupling tools, ready but not told when to act. Soft dawn light, steam and mist over the yard, calm administrative mood. Labels: "MIN 1" at the single coach, "MAX 20" at the end of the siding, "POLICY" above the separate rule book.

key: you set the target, and it works harder
name: ch10_ac_target_tracking
alt: An air conditioner set to 24 degrees works harder as a room fills with people in the afternoon heat and idles when the room is cool at night.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same office meeting room with a wall-mounted air conditioner and a small remote control lying on the table with a big display showing "24". LEFT panel: a hot afternoon; bright sun streams through the window, a dozen people crowd into a meeting, some fanning themselves with papers; the AC unit works hard, with strong blue airflow lines, a whirring icon and a small power meter beside it reading high. RIGHT panel: late evening; the room is empty except for a cleaner in a uniform with a mop, the window shows a dark sky and a moon; the AC hums gently with faint airflow lines and the power meter reads low. In both panels a thermometer on the wall sits near the same target mark. A small inset in the corner shows a sudden crowd bursting through the door and a delivery van labelled with a clock bringing an extra AC unit that will take a while to arrive. Contrasting warm and cool lighting, calm, practical mood. Labels: "TARGET" beside the remote's display, "BUSY" above the left panel, "IDLE" above the right panel.

key: at least one cook always on duty, never
name: ch10_restaurant_min_max_cooks
alt: A restaurant kitchen with one cook on a quiet morning and twelve cooks at a busy dinner, under a staffing rule board showing a minimum and maximum.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in the same restaurant kitchen with a long row of twelve stoves and twelve hooks for aprons on the wall. Above the doorway hangs a wooden staffing rule board showing a short bar with "1" at one end and "12" at the other. LEFT panel: an early quiet morning; a single sleepy cook in his 20s with a cap stirs one pot of poha at one stove, eleven aprons still hanging on their hooks, and one waiter yawning at the pass with a single order slip. RIGHT panel: a packed Saturday dinner; all twelve stoves are lit and twelve cooks of different ages work in a row, flames high, waiters rushing with plates; the manager, a woman in her 40s with a phone and a wallet bulging slightly, stands at the end of the row with her hand raised, firmly stopping a thirteenth eager cook at the door. A tiny thought bubble above the manager shows a calculator and a ledger. Morning daylight on the left, warm evening glow on the right, light humorous mood. Labels: "MIN" beside the single cook, "MAX" above the twelfth stove.

key: A lift operator who calls in an extra
name: ch10_lift_operator_cooldown
alt: An over-eager lift operator keeps calling and sending away lifts every time a couple of people wait, while a calmer operator waits a few minutes before each decision.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same office-tower lobby with a bank of four lifts and a small operator's desk with buttons. LEFT panel: a jittery young lift operator in his 20s in a uniform jumps up, pressing buttons frantically; lift doors open and close in a blur, lifts shoot up and down with many motion lines, and only two people wait in the lobby, looking confused; a small counter on the wall shows a huge number of starts and stops, and the operator sweats. RIGHT panel: a calm older operator in her 50s in the same uniform sits at the desk with a small sand timer beside the button panel, the sand running; she watches a moderate crowd gather, and only after the timer runs out does she call one more lift; the lifts move smoothly. In a tiny inset at the bottom right, the sand timer is huge and slow while a big crowd suddenly fills the lobby and looks impatient, hinting a too-long wait hurts too. Bright lobby lighting, light comic mood. Labels: "NO COOLDOWN" above the left panel, "COOLDOWN" above the right panel.

key: A home tiffin service. At first the cook
name: ch11_tiffin_service_four_stages
alt: The same home tiffin cook in four stages: doing everything by hand, following a fixed routine, tracking vegetable batches, and reviewing chats from an ordering bot.
scene: A four-panel strip read left to right, the same home cook in every panel, a cheerful woman in her 40s with a cotton saree, a bindi and her hair in a bun. PANEL ONE: she cooks, packs and rides off on a scooter with tiffins hanging from the handles, all alone and slightly frazzled. PANEL TWO: a neat wall chart with five steps drawn as icons, menu, cook, pack, check, dispatch, and a feedback box by the door; two helpers follow the chart calmly. PANEL THREE: she holds two tomatoes side by side, one pale winter tomato and one bright summer tomato, and writes batch numbers on crates in a register, a small thought bubble showing the same recipe tasting different. PANEL FOUR: she sits with a tablet showing a chat window from a friendly robot ordering bot; she reads replies, a red block stamp sits on one rude reply, and a row of thumbs-up and thumbs-down icons comes in from customers. A thin arrow runs under all four panels showing the progression. Warm kitchen light throughout, mood growing more organised from left to right. Labels: "DEVOPS" above panel two, "MLOPS" above panel three, "LLMOPS" above panel four; panel one has no label.

key: after computerised reservation
name: ch11_railway_paper_vs_computer
alt: Station clerks with separate paper charts double-book a seat, compared with one computer system that every station sees the same way.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: three separate small station booking offices shown side by side like islands, each with an old clerk in a white uniform and spectacles writing in a large paper reservation chart by hand; no lines connect them. Two passengers, a man with a tin trunk and a woman with a child, stand in a train coach holding paper tickets for the same seat number, arguing, a big question mark above them; long queues snake outside each office. RIGHT panel: the same three station offices now each have a computer terminal, and bright connecting lines run from all three terminals to one central server cabinet in the middle; every screen shows the same seat chart with the same seat marked booked. A printer in one office prints a ticket while a clerk in another office sees the update at once. A small inset at the bottom shows two of the clerks still turned away from each other with crossed arms despite the shared system. Faded, dusty light on the left; clean modern light on the right; mood moves from chaos to order. Labels: "BEFORE" above the left panel, "AFTER" above the right panel.

key: A cricket season: plan the squad
name: ch11_cricket_season_devops_loop
alt: A circular loop of cricket season stages from planning the squad to studying match footage, which feeds back into the next plan.
scene: A large circular loop drawn on a cricket ground, seen from above, with eight small scenes placed around it like stations on a clock face, connected by a curved arrow that runs clockwise. TOP: a coach in a team tracksuit and a captain plan the squad on a whiteboard with magnets. Clockwise: players practise in the nets with bowling machines; a selector holds up a team sheet picking the playing eleven; a warm-up match on a small ground; a press conference where the captain announces the team to reporters with microphones; the main match in a packed stadium with a batsman hitting a shot; a physiotherapist and team manager tending to players in a dressing room during the tournament; an analyst in a dark room studying match footage on a laptop with graphs. From the analyst, the arrow sweeps back to the planning whiteboard at the top, completing the loop. In the centre of the circle, a tiny clock spins fast with many little loops drawn around it to hint the software version runs many times a day. Bright sunny daylight, energetic sporting mood. Labels: "PLAN" at the top scene, "DEPLOY" at the main match, "MONITOR" at the analyst.

key: A masala brand. The recipe card
name: ch11_masala_recipe_harvest_batch
alt: A masala factory where the recipe card, this season's spice harvest and the resulting labelled batch are shown, and a new harvest changes the taste.
scene: A small masala factory with grinding machines, sacks and jars, shown as a left-to-right flow. LEFT: a recipe card pinned on a board with a list of spices and quantities, a master blender in his 50s in a white coat and cap tapping it with a pen. CENTRE: two piles of spice sacks, one marked with a sun icon for this season's harvest and one with a rain cloud for last season's, the chillies in this season's sack visibly a deeper red; a farmer in a turban unloads the new sacks from a cart. RIGHT: two finished jars of masala on a testing table; a taste-tester, a young woman in a hairnet and apron, tastes from the new jar and raises an eyebrow, while a worker relabels it with a new batch sticker. In a small inset above, a new recipe card is swapped in and a fresh third jar appears even though the sacks are the same. In another tiny inset at the corner, a customer at a shop shelf now reaches for a milder jar, shifting taste without the masala changing. Warm, spice-hazed light, earthy colours, industrious mood. Labels: "CODE" by the recipe card, "DATA" by the sacks, "MODEL" by the finished jars.

key: A hospital where the lab tests a blood
name: ch11_hospital_lab_barcode
alt: A lab technician shouts a blood result down a corridor, compared with a lab where every sample has a barcode and every result is logged and shown on the doctor's screen.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves set in the same hospital with a lab at one end of a corridor and a doctor's room at the other. LEFT panel: a harried lab technician in a white coat leans out of the lab door holding a test tube and shouts down the long corridor, the shout drawn as a fading speech bubble with a few numbers; at the far end, a doctor cups her ear, unsure, while a ward boy carrying a tray walks between them and the numbers in the bubble get scrambled. RIGHT panel: the same lab, but every test tube in a rack has a barcode sticker; a technician scans one with a hand scanner, and a thin glowing line runs from the scanner to a screen in the doctor's room where the result appears next to the patient's photo and name tag; a tall archive shelf of labelled files stands beside the screen. The doctor, a woman in her 40s with a stethoscope, reads the screen calmly. Fluorescent hospital light, chaotic on the left, calm and reliable on the right. Labels: "SHOUTED" above the left panel, "TRACKED" above the right panel.

key: A big wedding caterer. The registry
name: ch11_caterer_mlops_components
alt: A wedding catering operation with a labelled cold room, a shared prep station, a register of recipes and suppliers, and a head caterer with a timetable directing each station.
scene: A large wedding catering setup behind a tent, shown in a cut-away overhead view with four zones around a central figure. CENTRE: the head caterer, a commanding man in his 50s with a moustache, a kurta and a whistle, holds a big timetable on a clipboard and points at different zones, dotted arrows from him reaching each station. TOP-LEFT: a walk-in cold room with steel shelves where finished dishes in large containers sit with clear labels and dates, a worker placing a new labelled pot on a shelf. TOP-RIGHT: a long prep station where helpers wash and cut heaps of onions, tomatoes and coriander once, then send the cut vegetables in bowls to several different cooking lines. BOTTOM-LEFT: a desk with a fat register where a clerk in spectacles writes which recipe and which supplier went into each dish, with small supplier stamps on the page. BOTTOM-RIGHT: the cooking area with big handis on fires, a cook waiting for his cue from the head caterer. Warm evening light from strings of bulbs, busy and orchestrated mood. Labels: "REGISTRY" above the cold room, "FEATURE STORE" above the prep station, "ORCHESTRATOR" beside the head caterer.

key: A good pharmacy chain: medicines
name: ch11_pharmacy_six_principles
alt: A well-run pharmacy with automatic restocking, batch numbers on every strip, supplier records, delivery quality checks, expiry tracking and identical tablets every time.
scene: A wide view of a bright, well-organised neighbourhood pharmacy with a glass counter and tall shelves of medicine boxes, laid out so that six small activities are visible at once. LEFT: a delivery van at the back door where a robot-like trolley automatically refills an empty shelf slot. Behind the counter: a pharmacist in her 30s in a white coat holds up a medicine strip to show its printed batch number, magnified in a small inset bubble. On a side desk: a ledger open to a page comparing two suppliers' batches with ticks against one. At the delivery door: a young assistant with a checklist opens a carton and inspects strips under a lamp. Near the shelves: an older pharmacist with spectacles scans a shelf for expiry dates and pins a customer complaint slip to a board. In the foreground on the counter: two tablets from two different boxes sit side by side, looking exactly the same, on a small balance that is perfectly level. Clean, cool white lighting, calm, trustworthy mood. Labels: "VERSIONING" beside the batch number inset, "TESTING" beside the inspection, "REPRODUCIBLE" beside the matching tablets.

key: Opening a dosa stall. The cook
name: ch11_dosa_stall_three_roles
alt: At a new dosa stall, one person perfects the batter, another sets up the menu and billing, and a third arranges the space, gas, electricity, licences and a second stall.
scene: A street-food dosa stall being set up on a busy corner, shown with three people working in three zones from left to right. LEFT: a focused cook in his 30s in a vest and a towel on his shoulder tastes batter from a steel bucket, several small test dosas lined up on a griddle, each slightly different, with a notebook of ratios beside him. CENTRE: a young woman in a T-shirt and jeans arranges a printed menu board above the counter and sets up a billing machine with a QR stand and an order slip printer, a small tablet showing incoming orders. RIGHT: an older man in a shirt with a folder of papers negotiates with a landlord, carries a gas cylinder on a trolley, plugs in an electric connection and holds a licence certificate, while in the background a second identical stall is being assembled across the road as the queue grows long. In a small inset at the bottom corner, one single person in a cap does all three jobs in a tiny stall, juggling a ladle, a billing pad and a gas cylinder. Bright morning light, busy start-up mood. Labels: "DATA SCIENTIST" above the cook, "ML ENGINEER" above the woman, "MLOPS" above the older man.

key: Building a car factory vs. opening
name: ch11_car_factory_vs_garage
alt: A huge car factory that only a few companies can afford, beside many small garages fitting seat covers, tuning engines and adding music systems to those cars.
scene: A wide landscape split into a distant background and a lively foreground. BACKGROUND: one enormous car factory with tall chimneys, robotic arms visible through glass walls, an endless line of identical new cars rolling out of its gate, and a large price tag hanging from its roof; only one small boardroom window shows a few executives in suits. FOREGROUND: a long street of small, busy garages with roller shutters, each working on one of the cars from the factory. In the first garage, a young mechanic in overalls fits colourful seat covers; in the second, an older mechanic with a spanner bends over an open bonnet tuning the engine; in the third, a teenage apprentice installs a music system with speakers in the boot. A happy car owner in a cap waits outside with tea. A dotted arrow runs from the factory gate to the garages. In a small inset, a mechanic shrugs at an engine block that is sealed shut, showing he cannot change how it was built. Bright daylight, workshop grease and colour, practical mood. Labels: "PRE-TRAINING" above the factory, "LLMOPS" above the garages.

key: One rating means little; thousands
name: ch11_ratings_pile_feedback
alt: A single thumbs-down after one order means little, but a restaurant owner studies thousands of ratings to decide which dish to change.
scene: A split composition. LEFT third: a young man on his apartment balcony finishes a delivered meal and taps a single thumbs-down on his phone, a tiny lone icon floating up into the night sky and disappearing among the stars. RIGHT two thirds: inside a restaurant office after closing, the owner, a woman in her 40s with reading glasses and a dupatta, stands before a big wall board covered with thousands of small thumbs-up and thumbs-down icons grouped by dish: a column for butter chicken mostly green, a column for paneer tikka with many red icons clustered together. She circles the paneer column with a marker while her head chef in a white jacket nods and takes notes. On the desk, one thumbs-down card is shown beside an empty card outline for the better answer, with a small question mark, hinting that a bad rating does not show what a good dish would be. Cool evening tones on the left, warm office light on the right, thoughtful mood. Labels: "ONE RATING" above the balcony, "THOUSANDS" above the wall board.

key: If a parcel is late you see which leg
name: ch11_courier_tracking_trace
alt: A courier tracking timeline across a map with a pickup, a hub, out for delivery and delivered, where one slow leg is highlighted, plus a delivery boy calling and climbing stairs.
scene: A wide horizontal composition laid out like a journey along a road from left to right. LEFT: a courier picks up a parcel from a small shop counter, a little time tag above reading "10:02". CENTRE-LEFT: a large sorting hub with conveyor belts and stacked parcels, time tag "11:40". CENTRE-RIGHT: a delivery boy in a uniform polo and cap rides a scooter loaded with parcels through traffic, time tag "15:10"; this stretch of the road is long and coloured red, with a small traffic jam, a stopwatch icon above it showing it took the longest. RIGHT: an apartment building where the same delivery boy is shown twice: first on the ground making a phone call to the customer, with a small ringing phone icon, and then climbing the stairs briskly with a parcel, motion lines behind him; at the top a smiling woman in her 30s opens the door, time tag "15:55". Above the whole road runs a thin tracking bar with four dots, the red section clearly marked. Bright afternoon daylight, clear informative mood. Labels: "TRACE" above the tracking bar, "TTFT" beside the phone call, "TPS" beside the stairs.

key: Moving your home kitchen business into
name: ch11_cloud_kitchen_move
alt: A home cook moves her business into a rented cloud kitchen with a storeroom, a labelled spice rack, a manager with a timetable and a warehouse, packing her setup into a standard container.
scene: A two-part composition. LEFT: a small home kitchen where a cook in her 30s, in a salwar suit with an apron, packs all her pots, tawa, spice tins and recipe notebook into a standard shipping-style container box on wheels with a plain sturdy lid and wheels. A dashed arrow carries the container out of her home door. RIGHT: a large rented cloud kitchen building in cut-away with several rooms. A storeroom with sacks and boxes on shelves. A tall spice rack with dozens of identical labelled jars arranged neatly, each jar marked with a small icon. A manager in a vest and cap holds a timetable clipboard next to a small warehouse corner and a lorry depot outside the back door where a delivery lorry waits. Her container is wheeled into an empty bay and opened, unpacking exactly the same layout as at home. On the building's front, a small board shows rent tiers with a free tier and a tiny limit sign. Bright daylight, sense of growth and order. Labels: "DATABASE" above the storeroom, "VECTOR DB" above the spice rack, "CONTAINER" beside the container.

key: stock register from a notebook at home
name: ch11_bank_locker_connection
alt: A shopkeeper moves his stock register from home into a rented bank locker with a number and key, while the locker room door is left open to anyone holding a key.
scene: A two-part composition read left to right. LEFT: a modest home where a shopkeeper in his 50s, in a kurta and spectacles, lifts a thick stock register from a cluttered table at home, a mouse peeking near the notebook. A dotted arrow carries the register to the RIGHT: inside a bank's locker room with rows of shiny steel lockers. The shopkeeper places the register inside his locker, holding a key and a small card with a locker number written on it; the number and key together glow softly to show they are the connection details. The heavy locker-room door behind him stands wide open to the corridor, with a sign hung on it showing an open globe, and several strangers in the corridor could walk in if they held a key; one shady figure in a cap is shown jingling a ring of keys. A security guard dozes on a stool beside the open door. A small inset in the corner shows a bank teller checking a customer's face against a photo, contrasted with the open door. Cool bank lighting, slightly cautionary mood. Labels: "CONNECTION STRING" beside the number card and key, "OPEN ACCESS" above the open door.

key: catalogue moved from a card cabinet
name: ch11_library_online_catalogue
alt: A library replaces its wooden card catalogue with an online catalogue, opened with a library card, and a desk sign tells readers to use the online one now.
scene: The front hall of a public library with tall shelves and arched windows, shown in a medium-wide shot. LEFT: an old wooden card-catalogue cabinet with many little drawers, being wheeled away by a librarian's assistant in a cardigan, a few index cards fluttering out. CENTRE: a new computer terminal on a desk showing a search page, its web address shown as a simple globe and link icon at the top of the screen. A college student in her 20s with a backpack holds up her plastic library card to a card reader beside the terminal, and a green light glows. On the front desk, a librarian in her 50s with a bun and a shawl places a small standing sign with an arrow pointing toward the computer and a tick mark, saying to use the online catalogue now. RIGHT: a small inset scene shows a lost library card on the floor and a librarian cutting it up and issuing a new one, with a warning that every door it opened must also be changed. Soft daylight through arched windows, calm modernising mood. Labels: "ENDPOINT" above the computer screen, "API KEY" beside the library card, "USE ONLINE" on the desk sign.

key: A wedding planned twice: once at home
name: ch11_wedding_home_vs_banquet_stack
alt: The same wedding menu is cooked at home by cousins in a family kitchen and at a banquet hall with its own kitchen, cold storage and staff, set up from one booking form.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, with one identical printed menu card floating at the top centre, overlapping both halves, connected by arrows to each side. LEFT panel: a crowded family home on the wedding eve; aunts and cousins in festive clothes cook in a small kitchen, a home fridge stuffed with sweets, a cousin washing vessels in a courtyard tap, a grandmother supervising from a chair. RIGHT panel: a grand banquet hall with a professional kitchen of steel counters, a large walk-in cold room and uniformed staff in caps; at the front desk, a hall manager hands the family planner a single booking form, and dotted lines run from the form to the kitchen, the cold room, the dining hall and the staff roster, setting them all up at once. At each room door in the right panel, a staff member shows a small permission slip to a guard before entering. Warm, cosy, cramped light on the left; bright, polished light on the right; celebratory mood. Labels: "DEFAULT STACK" above the left panel, "CLOUD STACK" above the right panel, "BOOKING FORM" beside the single form.

key: Sending a parcel through India Post.
name: ch11_post_office_image_push
alt: At a post office, a man packs a box, shows a temporary token at the counter, writes the full address, hands it over and receives a tracking number for the receiver.
scene: A busy Indian post office interior with a wooden counter, steel grille, red letter boxes and a wall clock, shown as a left-to-right sequence of the same customer, a young software engineer in his 20s in a T-shirt and backpack. FIRST: at a side table he packs items into a cardboard box with tape. SECOND: at the counter he shows a small temporary paper token with a timer icon to the clerk, an elderly man with spectacles and a pen behind his ear, while a big permanent ID card stays in his wallet. THIRD: he writes a long full destination address on the box with a marker, ending with a short tag word "latest". FOURTH: he hands the box through the window and the clerk stamps it. FIFTH: he walks out holding a receipt with a tracking number, which he sends to a friend on his phone. In a small inset at the top, a sticky label reading "latest" is peeled off yesterday's parcel and stuck on today's new parcel. Warm afternoon light through tall windows, orderly mood. Labels: "BUILD" above the packing table, "TAG" above the address writing, "PUSH" above the counter handover.

key: After cooking the dish once by hand
name: ch11_kitchen_automation_ci_ct
alt: A cook who wrote down her recipe hands it to staff, sets up a standing vegetable order, installs a kitchen camera and a bell that rings if something burns.
scene: A restaurant kitchen in a cut-away wide view. LEFT: the owner-cook, a woman in her 40s with an apron and a notebook, hands a neatly written recipe sheet to two young kitchen staff in caps, who start cooking exactly by the sheet. CENTRE-BACK: at the rear door, a vegetable vendor with a hand cart drops off crates of fresh produce on a regular schedule, a calendar on the door with every morning ticked, and a dotted arrow shows the produce going straight onto the staff's counter and into the cooking. TOP-RIGHT: a small security camera mounted in the ceiling corner, its field of view shown as a pale cone covering the stoves. RIGHT: a red bell on the wall wired to a smoke sensor above a frying pan that is starting to smoke, the bell ringing with zig-zag lines. In the foreground, the owner relaxes in a chair with tea, but beside her is a small pile of unsorted tasks with a note pinned on top, showing what was never automated still needs her. Warm, busy kitchen light, efficient mood. Labels: "CI/CD" above the recipe handover, "CT" above the vendor, "ALERT" beside the bell.

key: goes to the desk (PR). First a quick
name: ch11_newsroom_ci_pipeline
alt: A reporter's draft passes a private-info scan, grammar and style checks and a slow fact-check before a proof edition and the morning edition roll off the press.
scene: A newspaper office arranged as a left-to-right conveyor of desks, the same typed draft moving from desk to desk. FIRST desk: a young reporter in her 20s hands over a draft in a folder. SECOND desk: a clerk with a magnifier scans the page for phone numbers and private details, blacking out one line with a marker. THIRD desk: a copy editor in spectacles circles grammar mistakes in red. FOURTH desk: a style editor with a ruler checks spacing and headline fonts against a house style book. FIFTH desk: a fact-checker surrounded by thick reference books and a phone works slowly, a small hourglass beside him. Then a small printing machine prints a proof copy, which two senior editors read at a table. FINALLY, on the far right, a large printing press starts automatically as an approval stamp lands on the page, rolling out a long stream of morning newspapers. Warm lamp light, a slightly frantic newsroom mood easing into calm at the end. Labels: "TESTS" above the fact-checker, "STAGING" above the proof table, "PRODUCTION" above the big press.

key: Checking a wedding card before printing
name: ch11_wedding_card_format_vs_lint
alt: A printer checks a wedding card proof: one person fixes alignment and spacing while another finds a hall that does not exist and a name used before it is introduced.
scene: A small printing shop with stacks of colourful wedding invitation cards, a proof table under a lamp and a printing machine in the back. On the table lies a large ornate wedding card proof with gold borders and a simple floral motif and a marigold pattern along the edges. LEFT side of the table: a meticulous young designer in her 20s with a ruler and a set square nudges crooked lines of text into alignment, small arrows showing letters moving into neat columns and spacing evened out; the words stay the same. RIGHT side: the printing shop owner, an older man in his 60s with thick glasses and a pencil, taps two problem spots circled in red: a venue address with a small map inset showing an empty plot where no hall stands, and a name in the closing line with a question mark because it never appears in the opening line. Between them, the father of the bride in a kurta peers anxiously at the proof. Warm lamplight, festive colours, careful, slightly comic mood. Labels: "FORMAT" above the designer, "LINT" above the shop owner.

key: annual day. The workflow is the
name: ch11_school_annual_day_workflow
alt: A school's annual day programme sheet lists events run in separate halls at the same time, each with its own ordered items, and a borrowed lamp-lighting act.
scene: A school campus decorated for annual day with bunting and balloons, shown as a cut-away of two halls side by side with a corridor in front. In the foreground, the principal, a dignified woman in her 50s in a silk saree, holds a printed programme sheet with a date circled at the top. HALL A on the left: a group dance on stage, children in bright costumes, and beside the stage a vertical list of three small numbered cards in order: costume check, music cue, dance. HALL B on the right: a school play at the same moment, children in cardboard crowns and painted backdrops, with its own vertical ordered card list. In the corridor between the halls, a teacher carries a prop box from one hall toward the other, a small note stuck on it to show props must be handed over deliberately. On the left edge, a visiting teacher from another school brings a ready-made brass lamp and matchbox for the lamp-lighting ceremony, placing it on Hall A's stage. Bright festive daylight, joyful mood. Labels: "WORKFLOW" on the programme sheet, "JOB" above each hall, "ACTION" beside the borrowed lamp.

key: Two counters at a passport office
name: ch11_passport_two_counters
alt: At a passport office, a fast counter checks the form while a slower counter verifies records, both needing a green stamp, and an old token is cancelled when a corrected form arrives.
scene: A government passport service centre with a token display board, rows of plastic chairs and glass counters, shown in a wide shot. Two counters stand side by side in the centre. LEFT counter: a quick young officer in a uniform shirt runs her finger down an application form, checking boxes and flipping through attached documents, pulling out one photo that belongs to someone else; a small stopwatch above shows a short time. RIGHT counter: an older officer with spectacles verifies the same applicant's details against thick record books and a computer screen, a stack of folders beside him and an hourglass above showing it takes longer. Both counters have a stamp; an applicant, a young woman in a kurta with a file, waits in the middle until both stamps turn green, and a gate to the passport-issue desk opens only then. On the token board above, an old token number is crossed out and a new one lit when a man at the side hands in a corrected form. Bright fluorescent light, orderly bureaucratic mood. Labels: "QA" above the left counter, "TEST" above the right counter, "CANCELLED" beside the crossed-out token.

key: Printing a newspaper edition.
name: ch11_newspaper_dated_editions
alt: At a newsstand, every edition has its date printed, the newest hangs on a today hook, and a vendor pulls yesterday's paper from the dated pile when today's has a mistake.
scene: A street-corner newsstand early in the morning, seen in a medium shot. On the left side of the stall, a neat stack of past editions is sorted by date, each paper's date clearly printed in a corner and fanned slightly so dates are visible. On the right side, a metal hook labelled with a sun icon holds the single newest copy. The vendor, a wiry man in his 50s with a muffler and a pencil behind his ear, is lifting today's paper off the hook because its front page has a big red error mark, and replacing it with yesterday's copy pulled from the dated pile, a curved arrow showing the swap. In front of the stall, a jogger in a tracksuit grabs a paper from the hook without looking, while a careful retired man in a cardigan checks the date in the corner. A delivery boy on a bicycle arrives with a fresh bundle. Behind the stall, a chai stand steams and a stray dog naps under the counter, and the dated pile is held in place by a brick so no edition gets lost. Soft early morning light, misty street, calm routine mood. Labels: "COMMIT SHA" beside a printed date, "LATEST" above the hook, "ROLLBACK" beside the curved arrow.

key: security guard a sealed envelope
name: ch11_guard_sealed_envelope_secret
alt: A society security guard uses a key from a sealed envelope to let the plumber in without seeing the house papers, while outside visitors get no envelope at all.
scene: The entrance gate of an apartment society with a guard cabin, a boom barrier and a notice board, in a medium-wide shot. A homeowner, a woman in her 40s in a cotton saree, hands the security guard a sealed brown envelope through the cabin window. The guard, a middle-aged man in a khaki uniform and cap, takes out only a spare key through a small slit without opening the envelope fully; an inset bubble shows the rest of the envelope still sealed, with house papers inside drawn as faint shapes he cannot read. A thin arrow shows him walking with the key to open a flat's service door for a plumber with a toolbox. At the gate, two strangers from outside the society, a man with a clipboard and a teenager, are politely stopped by a second guard who shows empty hands, no envelope for them. In a small corner inset, someone quietly rewrites the guard's duty roster on the notice board, a warning sign beside it. Soft daytime light, secure but watchful mood. Labels: "SECRET" on the sealed envelope, "CD JOB" above the guard with the key, "FORK PR" above the stopped strangers.

key: A mango pulp factory line
name: ch11_mango_pulp_factory_line
alt: A mango pulp factory line from trucks delivering mangoes to a godown, through washing and sorting, recipe batch prep and cooking, to new stock on shop shelves.
scene: A long factory line seen from a high side angle, flowing left to right, in the golden light of mango season. FIRST: trucks piled with yellow mangoes back into a godown where workers unload them into large bins. SECOND: a washing and sorting station with water sprays and a conveyor, women in hairnets and aprons sorting mangoes into crates by size and ripeness. THIRD: a recipe bench where a supervisor in a white coat measures sugar and pulp into a labelled batch tray following a recipe sheet. FOURTH: big steel cooking vats with steam, a worker stirring and checking a thermometer, finished pulp poured into tins that are labelled and stored on a rack. FIFTH: a delivery van unloading the new tins onto a grocery shop shelf, while a shopkeeper removes old tins. Between each station, a crate fills up and a small green light switches on to start the next station. In a corner inset, a manager checks a gauge showing how many new mangoes arrived before starting the line. Warm golden light, busy, productive mood. Labels: "FEATURES" above the sorting station, "TRAIN" above the cooking vats, "DEPLOY" above the shop shelf.

key: Manual: you flip the switch
name: ch11_water_tank_motor_triggers
alt: A rooftop water tank motor started four ways: a hand switch, a society app signal, a 6 a.m. timer, and a float sensor that starts it only when the tank is low.
scene: An apartment building in cut-away, with a large water tank on the terrace and a pump motor at ground level connected by a vertical pipe. Around the motor, four ways to start it are shown as four small scenes with arrows leading to the motor's switch. FIRST: a man in a vest and lungi flips a big wall switch by hand. SECOND: a woman in her 30s on her balcony taps a society app on her phone reporting low water, a signal wave flying down to the motor. THIRD: a round timer dial mounted beside the motor, set to six in the morning, with a rising sun icon. FOURTH: on the terrace, a float ball inside the tank on a hinged arm; the water level is low, the float has dropped, and a wire from the float clicks the motor on; a small water-level gauge beside it shows a red low mark. In a corner inset, a timer dial spins wildly with a calendar showing the first of the month, the motor running non-stop and water overflowing off the roof. Morning daylight, practical, lightly comic mood. Labels: "API" by the phone, "SCHEDULE" by the timer, "WATCHER" by the float.

key: A Mumbai local vs. one long-distance
name: ch11_local_trains_vs_long_train
alt: Several local trains run separate routes and hand passengers over at junctions, while one long thirty-coach train stops entirely because one coach is stuck.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a horizontal line. TOP panel: a rail map seen from above with three separate short local train routes in different colours meeting at two junction stations; small local trains run on each line, and at the junctions passengers walk over footbridges from one train to another, carrying bags and briefcases. One local train on the green line has stopped with a small warning triangle, while the blue and orange trains keep running, and a station board clearly names the green line as delayed. BOTTOM panel: one very long thirty-coach train stretched across the whole width, all coaches packed; one coach in the middle has a broken wheel with sparks and a mechanic underneath it, and the entire train is halted; hundreds of passengers lean out of windows looking frustrated, and the station display shows only a vague single message about the train being late. On the platform beside the long train, a big single start button on a pillar is shown, simple and tempting. Daylight, crowded rail energy. Labels: "PIPELINES" above the top panel, "MONOLITH" above the bottom panel.

key: A hospital patient file. Each department
name: ch11_patient_file_trace_stamps
alt: A patient's file travels from reception to lab, X-ray and doctor, each stamping what came in, what went out and the time, with a feedback form stapled at discharge.
scene: A government hospital shown as a left-to-right series of departments along a long corridor, a single patient file carried by a ward attendant in a uniform from room to room. FIRST: reception, where a clerk stamps the file cover with a time stamp. SECOND: the lab, where a technician in a white coat records a blood test and stamps the inside page with in, out and time columns. THIRD: the X-ray room, where a radiographer holds up a chest film and stamps the next page. FOURTH: the doctor's room, where a doctor in her 40s with a stethoscope writes a prescription and stamps the final page. Each stamp is drawn as a small coloured block on a timeline strip printed across the bottom of the file. FIFTH: the discharge desk, where a feedback form with a smiley scale is stapled to the file and a ward name tag is written on the cover. In a small inset, one department's room has no stamp on the strip, yet a blank gap still sits on the timeline showing the time it took. Clean hospital daylight, orderly mood. Labels: "SPAN" above one stamp, "TRACE" above the whole file, "FEEDBACK" beside the stapled form.

key: A pressure cooker whistle.
name: ch11_cooker_whistle_alert
alt: A cook relaxes in another room while a pressure cooker's whistle signals done, and a safety valve hisses when something goes wrong.
scene: A home kitchen opening onto a living room, shown in a wide cut-away. In the kitchen, a pressure cooker sits on a gas stove. LEFT half of the kitchen scene: the cooker whistles with a cheerful puff of steam and musical lines; in the living room a woman in her 30s in a salwar suit sits relaxed on a sofa reading a book, not watching the cooker, and lifts her head with a smile at the sound, a small green tick bubble beside her. RIGHT half: a second cooker on another burner hisses sharply from its safety valve with a red jet of steam and a warning bubble; a burnt smell is shown as dark curly lines; she rushes toward it in a later pose. Above the hissing cooker, a small inset bubble shows a pinned note card with a link icon pointing to a notebook of what happened, since the hiss alone cannot say why the dal burned. On the kitchen counter beside the stove lie a ladle, a bowl of chopped onions and a wall calendar, and through the window a neighbour's balcony with drying clothes is visible. Warm kitchen light, homely, mildly suspenseful mood. Labels: "SUCCESS" above the whistling cooker, "FAILURE" above the hissing valve.

key: Running a restaurant kitchen, not
name: ch12_contest_dish_vs_restaurant
alt: A chef holding a cooking-contest trophy for one dish, beside a running restaurant kitchen with recipe files, a morning prep routine, tasting notes, safety checks and a returned-plates watcher.
scene: A split composition divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT third: a cooking contest stage with bright spotlights, a young chef in his 20s in a spotless white jacket holding a golden trophy above a single beautiful plate of biryani, judges clapping behind him. RIGHT two thirds: the back of a real, working restaurant kitchen at dawn, the same chef now older and calmer, surrounded by six small activities. A shelf of numbered recipe binders with dates on their spines. Two helpers chopping vegetables by a morning prep checklist pinned on the wall, every box ticked. A small tasting notebook open on the counter with notes and scores for trial dishes. A food-safety inspector in a hairnet checking fridge temperatures with a probe. A waiter returning a half-eaten plate to a window where a supervisor makes a mark on a tally board. And two cooks at two stoves making the same dal from the same recipe card, their pots looking identical. Spotlight glare on the left, calm warm morning light on the right, steady professional mood. Labels: "ONE DISH" above the contest, "RESTAURANT" above the kitchen, "SAME DAL" between the two pots.

key: Every night the presses run
name: ch12_presses_ct_vs_cicd
alt: Printing presses run every night with the day's stories, a redesigned layout template is proof-checked before being installed, and a sales drop triggers a special edition.
scene: A large newspaper printing hall at night, shown in a wide cut-away with three zones. LEFT: giant rolling presses running automatically, fed by a conveyor of today's stories arriving as fresh pages from the newsroom above, with a moon visible through a high window and a calendar showing each night ticked; a single technician in overalls watches calmly. CENTRE: on a raised platform, two editors in their 40s, a man in a waistcoat and a woman in a sari with spectacles, examine a large new layout template sheet on a light table, marking it with a proof stamp, and a forklift waits to carry the approved template plate down to the presses. RIGHT: a sales manager's office with a wall chart showing a sharp drop in a line, a manager in a tie picking up a red phone, and a dotted arrow from the phone back to the presses where a smaller special-edition run starts. In the foreground, a bundle of fresh papers rolls off the press, each copy slightly different from yesterday's stack beside it. Moody night lighting with bright work lamps, industrious mood. Labels: "CT" above the presses, "CI/CD" above the template table, "MONITORING" above the sales chart.

key: A railway timetable. The printed
name: ch12_timetable_versioning
alt: A railway office with a printed timetable edition, small correction slips, train rakes with numbered maintenance logs, and yearly passenger count files.
scene: A railway divisional office beside a yard, shown in a medium-wide shot. On the left wall, a large printed timetable booklet hangs open with a bold edition number on its cover, and a clerk in his 50s with spectacles pastes a small correction slip onto one page, a little stack of earlier slips numbered in order on his desk. Through a big window in the centre, a train yard shows several rakes of coaches parked on tracks, each with a painted number on its side; a mechanic in a cap holds a logbook for one rake, open to dated entries, and a thin line connects the rake's number to its logbook. On the right, a tall steel almirah holds boxed files labelled by year, with a planner in her 30s pulling out one year's passenger counts. Beside the almirah, a small inset shows a huge warehouse full of identical boxes, hinting much bigger data is stored differently. Soft daylight, dusty paper smell implied, orderly administrative mood. Labels: "RELEASE" on the timetable cover, "COMMIT" beside the correction slip, "DATA VERSION" above the yearly files.

key: Each net session is an experiment
name: ch12_selector_notebook_tracking
alt: A cricket selector records every net session in a notebook, then at selection time sorts players by economy for a short match or wickets for a long one.
scene: A split composition divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: cricket nets on a sunny afternoon; a bowler in white bowls to a batsman while a grey-haired selector in his 60s, wearing a hat and a blazer, sits on a folding chair with a thick notebook on his knee; each row of his notebook has columns drawn for bowler, pitch, overs, wickets and economy, and he writes a new row as the ball is bowled; a thin arrow goes from the bowler into the notebook. A second bowler in the next net has no one watching, and his figure is faint and fading, showing an unlogged session is lost. RIGHT panel: the selection committee room with a long table; the same selector opens the notebook and sorts rows into two piles, one pile under a small short-match card with a stopwatch icon picking lowest economy, the other under a long-match card with a five-day calendar icon picking most wickets; other selectors lean in over his shoulder. Bright afternoon sun on the left, warm indoor light on the right, careful, thoughtful mood. Labels: "EXPERIMENT" above the nets, "TRACKER" beside the notebook, "SELECT" above the committee table.

key: Building a house. Unit tests check
name: ch12_house_test_pyramid
alt: A house under inspection at every level: bricks checked one by one, a wall tested as a unit, the whole house checked, the owner's walk-through, a monsoon storm and a re-check of an old leak.
scene: A newly built two-storey house in a suburban plot, with six inspection scenes arranged around it like a pyramid from bottom to top. BOTTOM: a mason in a vest taps individual bricks on a pile with a small hammer, setting aside a cracked one. Above that: an engineer in a hard hat pushes against a finished wall with a window frame, checking bricks, mortar and frame hold together. Next level: a plumber opens a tap, an electrician flips a switch and a light glows, and a carpenter swings a door, the whole house working. Above that: the owner couple in their 30s, holding the building plan, walk through the living room ticking a checklist. At the top: dark monsoon clouds pour heavy rain on the house while it stays dry inside. To the side: a worker with a torch re-inspects an old damp patch on the ceiling after a repair, a small circular arrow showing he does this after every fix. A faint pyramid outline links the scenes from wide base to narrow top. Mixed daylight and stormy light, thorough, reassuring mood. Labels: "UNIT" beside the bricks, "INTEGRATION" beside the wall, "REGRESSION" beside the old leak spot.

key: Checking a pressure cooker at the shop
name: ch12_cooker_black_box_test
alt: In a utensil shop, a tester heats a closed pressure cooker with a measured amount of water and checks that it whistles at the right pressure, including an empty-cooker case.
scene: A busy utensil shop with steel vessels hanging from hooks and stacked boxes of cookers, shown in a medium shot. At a test counter, a young shop assistant in a polo shirt and a lanyard tests a new pressure cooker on a small gas burner. The cooker's lid is shut and sealed; the valve mechanism inside is drawn as a dark, closed shape with a small padlock, untouched. On the left, a measuring jug pours an exact amount of water in, and a flame dial shows a set heat level; these inputs are marked with an arrow pointing into the cooker. On the right, a pressure gauge on a stand rises to a marked line just as the whistle blows a puff of steam, and an arrow points out of the cooker to a green tick on a checklist. Beside the main test, a second smaller cooker sits on the burner with no water inside, a dry interior shown in a cut-away bubble, its row on the checklist marked as the special empty case. A customer couple in their 50s watch, impressed. Bright shop lighting, practical mood. Labels: "INPUT" by the jug and flame, "OUTPUT" by the gauge and whistle, "EDGE CASE" by the empty cooker.

key: A ration shop weighing and inspecting
name: ch12_ration_shop_grain_checks
alt: A ration shopkeeper weighs and inspects sacks of grain, setting aside an underweight sack, one with stones and a damp one before stocking the shelf.
scene: A government ration shop with a tin roof, a big platform scale and shelves behind a counter, seen in a medium-wide shot. A delivery cart unloads several jute sacks of rice and wheat. The shopkeeper, a careful man in his 50s with a white cap and spectacles, weighs each sack on the platform scale, and the needle on one sack points well below the marked line. His assistant, a young woman in a salwar suit, pours a sample of rice from another sack onto a steel plate, revealing small stones mixed in. A third sack shows a dark wet patch at its base with drips on the floor. These three sacks are moved onto a separate area marked with a chalk cross on the floor, while good sacks go onto the shelf where customers with ration cards are waiting. On the wall hangs a short checklist with three icons: a scale, a stone and a water drop. In a small inset, one sack with a hidden problem drawn as a tiny worm slips past because no rule on the checklist covers it. Warm daylight from the shop front, careful mood. Labels: "VALIDATION" above the checklist, "REJECTED" above the separate area.

key: Testing a new student by giving them
name: ch12_student_eight_questions
alt: A tutor gives a new student the same eight multiplication questions again and again, and the student's score climbs toward full marks on repeated attempts.
scene: A small home tuition room with a wooden table, a whiteboard and a ceiling fan, in a warm medium shot. A patient tutor in her 40s in a cotton kurta and spectacles sits across from a young student of about ten in a school uniform with a pencil. On the whiteboard behind them are exactly eight multiplication questions written in a grid. On the table lie several attempt sheets stacked like steps, each with the same eight questions; the first sheet shows mostly crosses, the next more ticks, and the top sheet all eight ticks, a small rising line drawn over the stack. The student beams. In a small inset bubble on one side, a second student stares out of the window ignoring the questions, his sheets showing crosses every time, and another inset shows a smudged answer key with a wrong number circled. In another tiny inset, the happy student meets a ninth, new question on a card and frowns, hinting the memorised eight do not prove real understanding. Afternoon sunlight through curtains, encouraging mood. Labels: "OVERFIT" above the stack of sheets, "CAN LEARN" beside the smiling student.

key: trained before a new flyover opened
name: ch12_new_flyover_wrong_eta
alt: A navigation app trained before a new flyover opened keeps predicting long times for the old route, while cars zip over the flyover and a commuter shrugs at the wrong estimate.
scene: A busy city junction seen from slightly above, with a brand-new concrete flyover arching over a crowded old road below. On the flyover, cars and scooters move fast with motion lines; ribbon and marigolds from the inauguration still hang on its railing. Below, the old road is jammed with buses and autos. In the foreground, a commuter in her 30s on a scooter, office bag slung across, has stopped at the side and looks at a phone holder on her handlebar; an enlarged screen bubble shows a generic map app with the route drawn along the old road and a big wrong estimated time, while the flyover is missing from its map entirely. She shrugs and turns toward the flyover ramp. Nothing on the phone shows an error; the app looks perfectly normal and confident. In a small corner inset, a small control room shows a technician watching a graph of prediction errors starting to rise. Bright morning light, urban bustle, ironic mood. Labels: "STALE MODEL" beside the phone screen, "NEW FLYOVER" on the flyover.

key: career average vs his last 5 innings
name: ch12_career_vs_last_five
alt: A veteran batsman walks back after a low score while a stadium screen shows his steady career average beside a sharply falling last-five-innings figure.
scene: A cricket stadium at the end of an innings, seen from the boundary. In the foreground, a veteran batsman in his early 30s in a white kit and helmet tucked under his arm walks back to the pavilion with his head down, bat dragging slightly. Behind him, a huge stadium screen shows two side-by-side panels. The left panel shows a long, flat, steady line over many seasons with a small trophy icon, barely dipping at the very end. The right panel shows only five bars, each shorter than the last, with the final bar tiny and red. In the stands, two fans in team jerseys point at the right panel and argue, one worried, one dismissive. A small inset bubble in the corner shows a single bad bar being blown out of proportion by a commentator with a megaphone, hinting a very short window is noisy. On the field behind him, the next batsman jogs out swinging his arms, and a groundsman waits by the roller near the boundary rope. Late afternoon golden light, long shadows, slightly melancholy mood. Labels: "LONG WINDOW" above the left screen panel, "SHORT WINDOW" above the right screen panel.

key: A size-recommendation model for an
name: ch12_kurta_size_shift
alt: A kurta store's size advisor trained on one city's shoppers keeps suggesting the same sizes as the store goes national and taller shoppers try on kurtas that do not fit.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a single-city kurta store's trial room area; a row of shoppers stands against a height chart on the wall, mostly of similar medium height; a friendly robot-like size advisor on a kiosk screen recommends sizes, and the shoppers smile in well-fitting kurtas. A small curve icon above the height chart shows a narrow hump. RIGHT panel: the same store now with a national map on the wall and shoppers from many regions, a much wider range of heights against the same chart, from short to very tall; the kiosk screen still confidently shows the same size buttons; a tall young man stands in a kurta that ends far above his knees with sleeves too short, looking at himself in the mirror in dismay, and a short woman swims in an oversized kurta. The curve icon above the chart is now wider and shifted right. In the corner, a tailor with a measuring tape around his neck shakes his head knowingly. Bright retail lighting, gently comic mood. Labels: "ONE CITY" above the left panel, "NATIONWIDE" above the right panel, "SHIFT" beside the moved curve.

key: A sorting machine at a post office
name: ch12_sorting_machine_new_bin
alt: A post office sorting machine with letter and parcel bins forces padded envelopes into the wrong bin, then adds an other bin, then a proper new bin.
scene: A three-panel illustration of the same post-office sorting machine, read left to right, each with a conveyor belt feeding items into bins below. LEFT panel: only two bins exist, one with a letter icon and one with a box icon; flat padded envelopes ride the belt and get shoved into the letters bin, where they jam and bulge out, and a postal worker in a khaki uniform frowns, hands on hips. MIDDLE panel: a third bin with a question-mark icon has been added; the padded envelopes now drop into it and sit there unsorted, and the worker shrugs, half-satisfied. RIGHT panel: a proper new bin with a padded-envelope icon has been fitted, and the envelopes slide into it neatly; beside the machine, a supervisor in her 40s holds a stack of labelled sample envelopes she used to teach the machine, and the worker gives a thumbs-up. Courier vans are visible through a back door unloading more envelopes. Bright warehouse lighting, light industrial mood. Labels: "WRONG BIN" above the left panel, "OTHER" above the middle panel, "NEW CLASS" above the right panel.

key: Predicting auto-rickshaw demand.
name: ch12_auto_demand_three_drifts
alt: Three panels of auto-rickshaw demand: a new metro slowly drawing riders away, a fuel price hike emptying the stand overnight, and festival season crowds returning every year.
scene: A three-panel illustration of the same auto-rickshaw stand outside a suburban railway station, read left to right, with the same auto driver in each panel, a man in his 40s in a khaki uniform and a moustache. LEFT panel: a new elevated metro line is being completed in the background, and across a series of small calendar pages the queue of waiting riders at the auto stand gets shorter month by month, people walking toward the metro station steps; the driver scratches his head. MIDDLE panel: a petrol pump sign beside the stand shows a big upward arrow in red, and overnight the stand is nearly empty, autos parked in a long idle row, the driver sitting on his seat reading a newspaper. RIGHT panel: festive lights and marigold strings, a wedding band passing, families with gifts crowding the stand, and a calendar on the wall showing the same festival circled for several years in a row; the driver happily waves passengers in. Small trend icons sit above each panel: a gently falling line, a sudden cliff and a repeating wave. Varied light from grey to festive, informative mood. Labels: "GRADUAL", "ABRUPT" and "PERIODIC" above the three panels in that order.

key: weigh 100 from today and compare
name: ch12_laddoo_tray_weighing
alt: A sweet shop weighs a tray of today's laddoos and compares the spread with the standard batch, noticing the whole tray has shifted heavier.
scene: The back room of a traditional sweet shop with brass trays, glass jars and a big kadhai, in a warm medium shot. On a long counter sit two large trays of round yellow laddoos. The left tray is the standard reference batch with a small ribbon. The right tray is today's batch. A meticulous shop supervisor in his 50s, in a white kurta and a cap, weighs laddoos one by one on a small digital scale, and his assistant, a young woman with a hairnet, marks each weight on a chalkboard as dots on two rows. The reference row of dots clusters around a middle line; today's row of dots clusters noticeably to the right, the whole cloud shifted heavier. In a small inset, one single big laddoo sits alone on the scale with a shrug icon, showing that one heavy piece proves nothing. In another small inset in the corner, a taster in an apron tries a laddoo with several flavour icons floating around her head, hinting that flavour has many dimensions at once. Warm golden light, sugary steam, careful mood. Labels: "REFERENCE" above the left tray, "TODAY" above the right tray, "SHIFT" beside the dot rows.

key: dashboard warning light is monitoring
name: ch12_warning_light_vs_diagnostic_port
alt: A driver sees only an engine warning light on the dashboard, while a mechanic plugs into the diagnostic port and sees every sensor reading on a tablet.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves featuring the same small family car. LEFT panel: inside the car at night on a highway, seen over the driver's shoulder; the driver, a man in his 30s in a formal shirt, frowns at the dashboard where a single amber engine-shaped warning light glows, and nothing else tells him what is wrong; his wife in the passenger seat looks worried. RIGHT panel: a roadside garage the next morning; a mechanic in his 40s in greasy overalls kneels by the open driver's door and plugs a cable into a port under the dashboard; the cable leads to a tablet in his hand showing many small live readings, gauges for temperature, oil pressure, air flow and fuel mix, one of them flashing red; he points at it while the driver leans in, relieved to finally understand. Dark night with amber glow on the left, bright daylight in the garage on the right, problem-solving mood. Labels: "MONITORING" above the left panel, "OBSERVABILITY" above the right panel.

key: A lottery draw that uses a numbered list
name: ch12_lottery_seed_replay
alt: A lottery draw read from a numbered list instead of tumbling balls, which an official can replay exactly by using the same list again.
scene: A small stage at a village fair with festive bunting, set up for a lottery draw, shown in a split composition. LEFT side: a traditional glass drum full of numbered balls tumbles chaotically while a host in a sherwani turns a crank, and the crowd watches with excitement; a question mark hovers over the drum. RIGHT side: on a table, a thick printed booklet of numbered lists lies open, each page headed by a large page number; an official in her 40s with spectacles and a badge runs her finger down one page, reading out the numbers in order. Behind her, a second official opens an identical copy of the booklet to the same page number, reading the same numbers, and both their speech bubbles show exactly the same sequence, with a small equals sign between them. A villager in a turban at the front holds a tiny slip with the page number written on it, smiling as if he can replay the draw at home. Bright daytime fair light, playful mood. Labels: "RANDOM" above the drum, "SEED" beside the page number, "REPLAY" above the two matching officials.
